This is not only a gem in the rough, this is probably straight up one of the most amazing games ever made.
When I first saw news about this game about four years ago I was already hyped as fudge, checking for new articles and exclusive behind-the-scenes interviews on a daily basis. Now with the game released I have to say that this is the one game where the hype was justified and, even better, couldn't even shine enough light on the amazingness of this game.
It starts with the beautiful presentation in the main menu. You get a beautifully crafted minimalistic black and white background with menu buttons that use the same picture but stretched and scaled with a red tint. The "Option" menu has a "bake" option which I thought was a subtle and clever sociopolitical commentary on the corruption in the western world of capitalism.
Sound in this game is scarce, and rightfully so. The shots from your beautiful assault rifle -- definitely not a free stock model -- pierce the dark silence, accompanied by the red trace of the bullets. The two enemy types were scaring the bajeezuz out of me, especially the dark ones you can only notice from afar by their black smoke cloud. The tunnel parts of the game make for a nihilistic and dark expression of urban gentrification and fit very well in the open landscape hill sights. The last part of the game shines with a urban scenery and a final horde of enemies that will scare you to your bones. The intentionally left blank green pod in the end shines from afar, giving you a glimmer of hope (hence the color green). Once you reach this shining source of light you escape the hordes of demons and finish the game.
Impressed as I am? Use the hashtag #24724H to spread your love for the game and rise awareness of the impending doom of society as the game does. I must say that I don't think I have ever been so blown away in my life.

This game is weird, and that is awesome.
The concept of 'puzzle' in this game is the one of 'optimization,' because if you stitch here and there not really knowing what you are doing you can easily beat the first few levels of the game, but it becomes clear that you have to be more precise and intuitive if you want to get those three star ratings and finish the game! I definitely recommend this to people who are more used to puzzle games, but if you are looking for the most difficult of challenges, this may not be you...
..., unless you also like music! The musical aspect in this game is more robust than I expected (but I barely know anything about music theory or the sorts, just a heads up) and I enjoy it thoroughly. I felt like a kid again mixing and listening to my own ugly creations, and then editing them over and over; it never gets old for me when a game includs a creative aspect like this one.
That said, I do have some gripes with the game, like:
-how unwieldy the menus are while creating a song,
-not being able to add effects to single loops,
-not being ableto hear the song with all the elements while on the brain of a robot (edit: this is wrong, there is totally a way to do this c:),
-how the reading bar on the board takes too long to recognize a change or addition in the loop, and many other nitpicks.
The presentation is charming at its best, most of the time, and eerie at its worst, but I like it. Gives it a personality I've never seen other games even come close to achieveing.
This game is unique, fun and I love it.

This game is a must-have for any Game of Thrones fan. However, the game does have a few flaws, although these can really be overlooked most of the time.Warning, this is a long, long review. Minor spoilers below, not plot revealing spoilers in anyway, but do beware.
Gameplay: The gameplay of this game is not so much the kind you would expect in typical games nowadays - you won't find any of the running around. free-roam, hack and slash, resource gathering, or levelling systems you'd find in other games. This, like other Telltale Games is more of an interactive story as opposed to a Skyrim-esque hack-and-slash full on RPG. However, this doesn't mean there won't be combat or interaction in any way; quite the opposite, in fact. After accidentally triggering a fight between a group of bloodthirsty sellswords in a seedy bar (I swear it wasn't my fault), I found myself having to mash buttons at the speed of light, lest I get stabbed by said sellswords. The combat leaves much to be desired, but I didn't get this game because I wanted the best combat system in video game history. Most of the game itself revolves around your character's choices, and the characters you play are the members of House Forrester, a house once loyal to the Starks of Winterfell, whom after the Red Wedding are struggling to survive in the harsh rule of the Boltons, and their bannermen (who also happens to be the Forrester's worst enemies as far as anyone can practically remember), the Whitehills. Obviously, this game is set after and during the second half of 'A Storm of Swords' or for the show watchers (I know everything because I am a book reader :P) Season 3-4, so new show watchers or readers of the books will struggle to understand the character, so the game is only worth buying after you've seen or read past the Red Wedding (The North Remembers, ya damn Freys). The game itself doesn't have in any way the scantily-clad women (and men) as the show or the books, however it does have a good deal of violence and foul-mouthed characters, who if in anyway used that kind of language in front of my mother, would have their mouths washed clean with soap. The choices the players make will effect the way the other characters regard their character or even change the storyline entirely (although that's very rare and I don't think it has happened in any shape or form to me yet). The gameplay however is a solid mix of both wits and reflexes (those buttons have to be pressed quickly, you mark my words), and some choices will provide a better outcome for House Forrester than others. This is an episodic game, therefore, parts of the story are being released once in a while, usually once a month.
The Story: The story is great. Within the current four episodes, I really got to understand the motives and reasonings behind some of the characters. The plot is filled with so many murders and secret alliances that it seems like this is just another chapter of the books written by GRRM himself. The story had me rooting for the Forresters since the start, however I really got to sympathise with some characters, like Finn (although he's a bit of an♥♥♥♥♥ and Gryff Whitehill (even though he's a total jerk).
My complaints:
Sometimes, it felt as if the choices I made were useless, and didn't effect characters at all. The choices I made seemed to lead up to the same thing regardless of what I did. I couldn't save any characters who died despite playing my best and being diplomatic and friendly to their murderers. I'm really hoping this will change because I got really♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off when the little lord of House Forrester met the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of Bolton and I could do nothing. I also understand that it's an episodic game, but I wish that the episodes could be released faster or at least have us know when the episodes were released. There's no way to entertain yourself with this game other than repetitively playing the episodes over and over again while waiting between episodes. Maybe make it so that between episodes release a minor 'prequel' scene, maybe showing the events before the episode, or the events between cutscenes during the previous episodes, once every two weeks to keep the players entertained. Because so far, playing this game has consisted of:
a) Getting the episode and being real happy.
b) Playing it for a few hours or so.
c) End of episode, with some cliffhanger that gets you real hyped and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at the same time.
d) Mulling around and praying that the new episode is released for a month or two.
e) Getting the new episode and repeat from step a)
Final Thoughts: Despite the flaws this game has, it has kept me well entertained as a hardcore Game of Thrones fan myself. I think it's a great game, well worth your money. Final rating is 9/10

I have played this game throughout its time in Beta, and therefore have formed a few rudimentary opinions. TL/DR: Buy it if you're a casual gamer, but if you hate the thought of losing through things which aren't necessarily your fault, this isn't for you.
Firstly, there are many positive attributes to this game. These are: a good blend between building and combat, with what ultimately feels like two substantial halves, some good map diversity, and an enjoyable experience that can either end in 5 minutes of mayhem, or 30 minute long sieges with ridiculous defense lines. Both of these present their own challenges, and ultimately enjoyable experiences.
However, the game falls down in both its players and design elements. Firstly, I have found the community to be less than helpful, with toxic players often weighing down games. Beyond this, a lack of rating results in you often being saddled with players far below the average level. Characters suffer from being unbalanced, and the game itself has issues with queue times and a limited pool of players.
I think this game has potential to evolve into something great, and would personally say buy it, but given Jagex's record, dont expect them to listen to community advice anytime soon. Either way, if you're willing to cope with a sometimes toxic environment and losses you feel cheated on, this game is worth it's modest £10 price.

One of the most intricate and closest to proper roleplaying RPG I have played in a very long time. The amount of love and detail put into this game makes it a shining example of Kickstarter helping to create wonderful experiences.
You are able to properly roleplay your characters by making decisions or simply conversing and the (shift) of your personality will actively influence your character's attributes, if only in a minor way.
The combat is what you would expect from its turn-based nature, but the ability to manipulate your environment through the elements leads to many interesting combinations (i.e. cast a poison spell onto the ground and set the puddle on fire with a candle you mugged from a peasant's house to create a burning surface that will do huge amounts of damage to enemies who dare to cross it). You are also able to set up the battlefield in advance by moving around barrels or using all kinds of items that seem mundane at first. Or you skip the battles altogether, sneaking by most of your enemies and then using the teleporter stones to get your party back together. A trap exuding poisonous gas? Throw the Ham you stole from a tavern on it to block the vent.
The crafting system is also rather complex, despite the actual crafting being as easy and drag and dropping two items together. There is quite the impressive list of possible recipes, most found through books you find on your journey. Although personally I didn't dabble much with it on my first playthrough.
It took me 70 hours to complete the game, trying to solve every quest and explore every area, which is what I would expect from a role playing game of this calibre, and it did not disappoint. Although the world seems rather small (since there is only about 5 bigger maps which your party could cross in about 2 minutes) the sheer amount of hidden treasures, caves, secrets, quests and of course enemies make them feel packed and every bit of progress feels like an accomplishment.
The only downsides I'd personally see are a few things such as the persuasion system (which is just a game of rock-paper-scissors, which makes sense for the co-op idea of the game but if you're in single player or trying to persuade NPCs it's just pure RNG and begs for save scumming), the bartering system (again born out of the co-op nature of having separate inventories which makes it unnecessarily difficult if you have to move around items and money all the time), the world 'feeling' small (see above) and that ultimately, despite all role-playing, your characters are out to save the world and ultimately do so, no matter how selfish and uncaring you played them before.
Otherwise I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who is even remotely interested in a proper, solid and lovingly put together RPG. Don't miss out on this gem.

Begin EDIT ----------------- 17 Dec 2014
Before this edit, I could not recommend this game, not due to the game play, etcetera, but because I could not play it due to some form of hardware or software conflict. But, due to a comment left by deathdude311, I can now play the game.
Look below to see the various steps I took but could not get past a crash to desktop (CTD). The text below leads to this final troubleshooting step:
1.) Go to the Sound option on the Control Panel.
2.) Disable ALL drivers listed.
3.) Enter the game and launch any mission
(this is where I had my CTD 100% of the time, this time I successfully entered the mission.)
4.) Exit the game.
5.) Return to the Sound app on the Control Panel, reenabling the drivers you disabled earlier.
6.) Reenter game.
Tada!!! (^_^)
Now to play the game. I will leave an actual review later, after I recall why I loved this game sooo much (have long term memory issues).
Ending EDIT --------------- 17 Dec 2014
Well, I give up.
Purchase this game, Star Wars: Battlefront II, having owned it when initially released. Played it. Loved it.
Now, though, whenever I tried to enter a mission -- training, story or other missions -- the game would crash to desktop (CTD). Knowing this game was not designed with Windows 8.1, I went in an set compatibility mode Windows XP (Service Pack 3), then Service Pack 2. Both failed to fix the problem.
I went to the Community Hub and found others who ran into this problem. There were possible fixes listed. First fix was to hide any disabled drivers on Sound option on the Control Panel, plus to make sure that the speakers were set to stereo instead of surround sound or the like. Failed.
Someone mentioned the possibilty dropping the game into window mode, start a mission, the resetting full screen. No one seemed to know how to set the game to window mode. No window mode choice in Options. The old Alt+Enter key commination failed as well. So not having a way of beginning that branch of troubleshooting, I went on.
Someone mentioned plugging something into the mic outlet, not understanding why that should do anything, I hunted for a headset or speaker that was not USB. I knew I did not have a mic, and the individuals who mentioned this possible fix, said it did not matter what was plugged into the port, just something. Found a headset and plugged it into the front port on my computer, then the port on the back. Both failed.
Though not seeing this as a fix for this, I disabled Steam's ingame features. Again, no go.
I'm not sure if there were other fixes listed, but I did follow them all, none worked, of course.
I dropped by Lucasarts database to see if they had any possible fixes that I had not attempted, but there was nothing new.
I dropped by YouTube to see if there was something knew, but there wasn't, though I did find a possible cause for CTD: Battlefront seems to hate the sound card chip I have on my motherboard. He had two fixes. 1.) Get a Sound Blaster card. 2.) Plug something in the mic port.
There seems to be one item on the list of possible fixes that I have not tried: getting a Sound Blaster card. Cannot afford one now, but later I will drop in a sound card, and this MAY fix the problem.
Until that occurs, and it fixes the CTD, I am going to not recommend this game. The game is definitely good, but with my system, there is something that is conflicting with it and I cannot relive the joy of playing this game.
There are many who, through one fix or another, are enjoying this game now, just realize, there may be something in your computer that will not allow you to play Battlefront.

Yu-Gi-Oh on Steam? Am I dreaming? Nope, apparently it's not a dream. Just pinched myself :']
So what are my first impressions of the game?
PROS
- YGO ON STEAM!!!
- Responsive clicks & runs smooth (takes a tiny bit of getting used to right click to open phase menu)
- Can click and hold the right mouse button to negate the card activation popup from interrupting play if you don't want to activate any cards, which works well
- # of obtainable cards allow for plenty of creative yet functional deck building
- Aside from using a legacy deck in story mode you can use said self created decks in Campaign mode, which is nice
- The Generation Campaigns follow the key events from the Yu-Gi-Oh! anime, so you're in for a trip down nostalgia lane if you've watched that or can catch up with the story if you haven't
- Wooo, achievements & Steam trading cards!
CONS
- The Battle animations/sprites of YGO's most iconic cards look really bad in comparison to the graphics of some other Tcgs
- Published by Konami, and looking at the list of DLC tells you enough about their intentions
- Forced tutorial at the start of every Generation Campaign, very annoying if you're an experienced player
- The annoying robots from the latest console/mobile YGO releases are back again. Like really guys, can't you replace them with a hot girl character or something? I'll even take an Apache Helicopter at this point >_>
Also, despite claiming that this game has a brand new Story Campaign @About this game, it's mainly just a rehash again of key events from the YGO anime + free battles vs most characters from it, so don't expect a unique story like Reshef (ROD) or being able to roam free and challenge random duelists like in the story mode of the NDS World Championship games. The latest 5 or even more YGO games that Konami has published have been rehashes about the past/current generations, most of them not even containing a story (like Duel Generation, Millennium Duels etc). So you could say that they're not really trying anymore when it comes to European YGO fans atleast, which is a shame (Google what Konami did to the European release of Duel Carnival for the 3DS if you want to know the details).
All in all, this won't be the best YGO game that you'll ever play but it's really nice to atleast have it on Steam now. And while Konami might be bleh, from a real Tcg player perspective this is still the best card game out there. Forget Magic, forget Pokemon, forget Hearthstone, forget Shadowverse, forget all of them! They cannot top the one true king of Tcgs. And if you're new to YGO and don't know what I'm talking about when I say this, then buy this game and find out! ;)
P.S. If you like the gameplay mechanics of this then do yourself a huge favour and buy the GBA/NDS/3DS YGO games aswell. They are absolutely worth playing c: great way to spend time offline (so when you're travelling & don't have access to an internet connection or something, I dunno).

If you like brawl games (i.e: super smash bros), then this should be an automatic pickup. Great party game, simple yet deep gameplay, and great potential for mindgames and trickery at high levels of play once all the mechanics have been mastered. Be warned however, if you do not live in North America, South America or Europe you might struggle to find a game that isn't laggy if you venture into online multiplayer. If the lag passes a certain threshold, then a crash to the main menu is all but guaranteed. Trying to play too far outside of your continent's peak time (seems to be 8-10pm here in Europe) is an exercise in futility.
Pros:
- Perfect controller support
- Engaging, simple and deep gameplay.
- The community is eager to teach each other tricks, timings, openers, etc, making the learning curve much easier if you ask for help.
- Low skill floor, high skill ceiling.
- Very challenging singleplayer challenge mode.
- Singleplayer, multiplayer and local multiplayer modes.
Cons:
- Lag can become a serious issue if playing with people from a different continent.
- Tutorial leaves a lot to be desired. It misses one of the most important aspects of counter-play (the parry).
- Does not allow you to set a resolution in windowed mode (my biggest gripe with the game).
- Bots lack any non-essential movement (hitting corpses, moving back and forth to add extra visual noise, pre-positioning), making fights against them feel very static compared to players.
- Matchmaking in its current incarnation does not put you into a lobby that has already played a game and has no 2v2 option, making organizing games via steam community chat much better than the "quick match" button.
- No text chat in the lobby, making using the steam community chat even more vital.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is my first game of the series. I saw this game from a review by Totalbiscuit and had to pick it up. While the bugs have frustrated me occasionally, the experience watching my own squad essentially kill themselves from panic was worth it. I've gone through pain and misery watching 95% shots fail, and being ambushed by what felt to be an infinite amount of aliens pouring through the fog of war. Needless to say, I can't want for November 2015 when Firaxis releases XCOM 2.
The strategy behind this game goes in depth significantly. There are, to me, two stages of the game. One is managing your base and resources to work with, whether that be weapon development, buildings, and panic of countries. Focusing your resources to one area leaves the others weak, meaning UFOs can win in aerial battles, countries may panic more easily, or your soldiers may find themselves weak on weaponry in the battlefield. For many of the people here who want to hit 100% perfection on XCOM, good luck. This game is all about cutting your losses in the higher difficulties, and staying alive rather than going big for rewards.
Newcomers to XCOM, as well as veterans from the older games can come try this game out. It offers a skill cap that punishes mistakes quite hard, but not enough to discourage a newbie to keep pressing on. Being on your toes with strategy, movement, and the future of the XCOM project make the game very rewarding with one downside. Sometimes a plan won't go correctly, and you'll delude yourself into thinking the game is against you. The reality of XCOM is that you never had the odds on your side. The aliens have stronger weaponry and many times more numbers than you would ever have. To the newcomers of XCOM, I'd strongly recommend against downloading the acclaimed Long War mod, as it is massively more punishing in comparison to the vanilla game.
The amount of content in this game is insane. Without the Enemy Within DLC or the free Long War mod, the game can last over 100 hours on a single campaign run. Adding those two can bring the game to triple the length. Both these two additions bring increased depth to everything, from new weapon types and genetic/mech modifications to your soldiers. For Enemy Within, a third force that seeks to side with the aliens is also against you, and their purpose is to mess with you as hard as possible, draining your resources if left unchecked. Long War increases the difficulty up a notch by increasing the health of the aliens, as well as their numbers. I'd strongly recommend playing it on normal difficulty even if you have beaten the vanilla game on a higher difficulty.
Overall XCOM Enemy Unknown is a great experience to have. You build bonds with your squad, and can customize them to how you like them. Watching them grow and conquer aliens is amazingly fun, even if you have already beaten the game once or twice. The feeling of progression outside combat transitions to inside, with your soldiers adorning your dedication to researching new armors, weapons, and enhancements. The countries that contribute to XCOM's monthly budget reward your continued success with more resources, allowing you to proceed faster. All of this can go backwards as well, making XCOM an engaging challenge that any strategic gamer should take.

Overall it feels like a classic RTS from the 90's, early 2000's (C&C / RA / Dune). There are no special unit abilities which in my opinion adds more to the charm, each unit is strong and weak against another. The units themselve are very interesting in both design and how they move and for once we get to see the Humans as the more tech savvy fellows.
The tech tree is simplistic, you get to choose 1 out of 3 upgrades for each type of unit (light, heavy, air, economy) and each upgrade caters to your overall playstyle.
Base building and management is interesting and not hard to understand if you have played RTS games before (this apply's to the Human and Beta faction only).
The campaign is lengthy, fully voiced and interesting to boot. The missions for each faction can be easy or hard, some are quite challenging taking up to 1 or 2 hours to beat and even some restarts. Some of them are trial and error and that's the charm of them. I was never angry with loosing a mission and having to restart again, I learned the AI's tactics each time I restarted and adapted.
And of course, the soundtrack is amazing. But what else could you expect from Frank Klepacki.
However, for those that love to play multiplayer in RTS, the game currently has a max of 4 players on maps (ie 4 FFA or 2v2). Some consider this a negative point for the game, some do not.

The pros are all listed above, but I want to be a bit more in depth and explain why. I don't normally go into the story of the game and characters, because I think that you have to experience those things for yourselves, but I focus on the details and features of the game, so without further ado:
Storyline - Like I mentioned, the storyline is somewhat in-depth. There are many angles because there are A LOT of characters that you can play in this game. They are all connected and everything stays consistent with the storyline, as well as staying smooth. Having said that, you can predict what's going to happen most of the time and it's not amazingly epic, which doesn't leave a whole lot to your imagination, as far as the story goes. However, this isn't a big fault and can be enjoyed on your first play through.
Gameplay - You battle your way through dungeons to progress through the main story line and this is mostly what you'll be doing throughout the game. I'm not gonna lie, it does get a bit grindy, but at least what you are earning along the way is stuff you will need to build new weapons, armor, outfits, etc. The customization (which I will get to right after) is what allows the battles to stay new and re-invented. I recommend use a control for this game. The full controller support works just as it should and feels like it too! You'll see events, some videos, great artwork, and fitting music down the road.
Customization - This is really one of the key features of this game. There's a few different ways the game accomplishes customization:
1. Character outfits - All of the characters you play in this game are girls and they can wear MANY different costumes. As you are defeating enemies and finding items in dungeons, you will pick up some of them, some you will get plans for that you have to make with materials, and some you can buy in the shop on chapter intervals. They can wear anything from cosplay costumes to swimsuits, so go wild!
2. Battle Customization - One of the features that makes the continual battles less of a bore. There is room for strategy here. You are allowed to pick your follow up combo moves for regular attacks, which include: rush, power, and break. As you level, you will unlock more options and you can continue to find which moves work best on enemies, which fill your EXE drive faster, and which breaks the enemies' armor the quickest. You even unlock elemental combo moves to use for strategy!
3. Dungeon Customization - One of the cooler features about this game. You can actually add to a previously completed dungeon and add dungeons that are not normally part of the storyline, aka side-quest dungeons. Once you gather the appropriate materials and find the plans, you can add tougher enemies to a previous dungeon and add new items to the map. The new enemies drop new items as well and so you can go back and actually pick up new materials, outfits, plans, etc. While it doesn't COMPLETELY change the dungeon, it is definitely a good feature for revisiting dungeons for mats you may need and making it less of a chore.
4. HDD Customization - I haven't gotten into explaining what HDD is yet, but specific characters can access whats called HDD mode. It's comparable to going super saiyan, overdrive, trance, or whatever kind of mode you can think of in other games. Not only can you change your armor and looks, but it'll change your battle stats as well so you can be extremely powerful in this mode, as well as lookin hot in minimal amounts of clothing.
Dungeon Landscapes - When you enter a dungeon, it will have a certain theme. Industrial, nature, futuristic, etc. They are all done to a dramatic fashion. They look great and the aesthetics are actually immersive. Backgrounds, flooring, enemies, music, dungeon items; they're all specific to where you are and the dungeons just look great overall.
Colosseum Mode - Colosseum mode is a way to test your strength and pick up extremely powerful weapons, rare materials, new outfits, items, etc. It has level specific challenges in which you fight enemies, but you're fighting for lots of cash (credits) and the aforementioned rewards. These are actually a lot tougher than the enemies on the map and can provide a challenge for even those who are max level. You can also find plans to add new colosseum fights as you go throughout the game to keep the fun rolling.
Japanese Voice Acting - The japanese voice acting in this is amazing! The translation in English isn't always the best, but the japanese voice actors/actresses do an amazing job, putting emotion and soul into the characters. I laughed really hard at some of the ridiculous things that happen in this game, so I give credit to the voice actors/actresses for giving life to the characters. There are only a few male characters, but they are done well too.
Museum Mode - The small details is what can make a good game, a great game. Museum mode is a small detail, but I was very grateful it was there. Museum mode allows you to see the artwork that was shown to you throughout the game, whether it was a scene you encountered, concept art, game box art, or whatever the case, you can review them there. This means that if you liked a particular picture that showed up, you can go check it out in game and look at it for as long as you want. To go along with this, there is also space in the museum for a music box. If you loved the music during battles, in town, or around, check them out here without anything else clouding the music. ^_^
English Voice Acting - One of the WORST things i've encountered with this game. I had it set on English for voice in the beginning and it became extremely annoying, very fast. The English voice acting is cheesy, poorly done, and seems extremely fake to me. Luckily, the voice language and subtitle language are independent of each other, so it was a very fast fix. I switched to Japanese voice with English subtitles and found out how great the Japanese voice acting was. I would highly recommend switching languages as soon as you start the game.
Repetitive Dungeon Maps - One down side to the dungeons is that, although there are a lot of them and have different landscapes, the themes and maps can be extremely similar. Let's say you open up the first dungeon of the game and you find a spring theme. It looks great, but you'll eventually open up a side-quest dungeon that will have the same theme. At this point, you will be pretty much using the same exact map and seeing the same aesthetics. Unlocking new dungeons may ADD some land or areas that the older dungeon didn't have, but after seeing them all for the first time, it's hard to appreciate reusing the same stuff over and over again.
Grindy - For some people, this is actually a pro. I happen to love grinding mats, exp, money, etc. in games. However, if you are not one that likes grinding for these, this game probably isn't for you. You'll be battling for like 80% of the game and there are achievements that are available on steam for maxing the level of all the characters. This takes quite a bit of time, but if you can figure out how to properly farm exp, it's actually not too hard to max out your characters. I maxed everyone by chapter 6, I believe.
Overall, 8/10 for me.

Let's answer the question "Should you buy it?" right now:
Do you generally like anime?
Yes? Buy it.
No? Stay the ♥♥♥♥ away from this game.
Why?
Because this game is pretty much a playable anime. It has all the tropes, plot, and "plot ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)" that you'd find in pretty much all anime. However, it does certain things different from most generic anime that makes this game series stand out and end up being highly entertaining.
Now when you look at the screenshots, you might think, "oh, this is one of *those* games, along the lines of Huniepop and the Sakura games." Don't worry. It's not as bad as you might expect. While there's no doubt there's fanservice, it's never really the focus of the game. Most of the gameplay revolves around looking at the back of these characters, not the front, and you'll be focused on the action (think Kill La Kill but less smart about it). The other half of the game will be the visual novel part, which stays pretty mild most of the time.
The plot it's nothing too special. You have a world to save like pretty much every game out there, but this time you're a goddess...that's a anime waifu representation of consoles. The thing that stands out is the most is the actual dialogue. It's just funny and entertaining as hell and the characters are for more interesting when you pay attention to what they say vs what they are (most of them are fairly trope-y).
As for the gameplay, I haven't played many jrpgs so I can't say how good it is objectively, but I must say I found it fairly enjoyable. Essentially you position your characters to kill enemies with three different types of attacks. Your attacks can get upgraded different ways, either with elemental augments or with the most damage or hits. It gets repetitive, but I found it competent even though there's room for improvement.
The music is like the gameplay; it's repetitive, perhaps more so. But it's nice. It's catchy. I like the tunes and never found them annoying. It's love or hate.
I have two major cons though: manually saving only (aka no autosaving) and grinding. If you die, you get kicked back to the last time you made a manual save. This can ruin your playthrough so make sure you save very often. I did this on accident TWICE losing a good amount of progress and grinding. And grinding is necessary. When you reach the next story boss, they'll always be extremely tough to beat. This makes you required to constantly farm on enemies around your level so you don't get demolished in battle. Fortunately there are grinding guides, but it doesn't make it any less frustrating.
All in all, I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of anime in general. You don't have to be a  weeaboo to enjoy this, but even if you're just a casual fan and find the artstyle serviceable then you'll probably enjoy this. There's enough that differentiates it from most other anime and anime games that makes the game (and the rest of the series) from feeling generic or tripe.
The whole is greater than the sum of its parts.
TL;DR came for ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°), stayed for actually good gameplay and funny dialogue

The strategic elements of the game are not hard to grasp, but the amount of time added to the battles by the way they are designed just makes it unenjoyable for me. And when i am able to just shut down in a game it becomes pointless to me to be playing a game at all when i could watch a movie or tv show while i do chores...
I don't mind punishing gameplay, or difficult gameplay as long as there is some reward for breaking through it. But i'm also not the type of person who considers visuals/story/music "rewarding".
If you are, then this might just be your game, and if you want to support the devs (who i still do believe deserve it regardless of my annoyance) then definitely support them, But if you are a strategy fan who is looking for some gripping gameplay... Honestly, one of the best RPG games I have ever played and I play a lot of RPGs. If you are a fan in any way of old style RPG games or are just a RPG fan in general, you have to get this game. And even if you not a hardcore RPG fan, I really think that you can still have fun with it. I don't understand why its not more popular however this game deserves to be main stream all the way.
Pros:
- Awesome combat which makes you think before you enter combat situations and really rewards you for eating food which gives you buffs.
- No hand holding what so ever therefore making the game challenging but still a lot of fun
- Game is long! Finally a game worth the price... I didn't think those existed any more.
- Awesome story line that im not where near to finishing but am enjoying so much.
- Awesome interaction with the citizens around the city and an all around immersive RPG style game.
- Multiplayer is awesome!
(Many, many more Pros but I don't want to go on forever)
Cons:
- The game may not be updated as frequently as most would like.
- There is the possibility that you may miss a quest item completely and you may not be able to retrieve this item literally making the game unbeatable, which would make some people mad... but hey pay attention and you should be fine.
- Same goes for if you kill an NPC. The NPC might be a quest giver or required for a quest later in the game.
- You really have to read up on the forums and research different builds and watch How-Tos... A lot.
- Even though Multiplayer is awesome, its only two player, however you can easily download one of the many four player mods out there. I think there is even one on the steam workshop now. Should be easy to find and install.
Even with these Cons, this game is so worth it and if you weren't convinced of buying this game before, I really wish that this review convinces you.

A review for older gamers: IF YOU LOVED URKEL, THIS GAME MIGHT BE FOR YOU!
Remember Urkel from TV? His strange voice always sounded forced and unnatural. Like it was "supposed" to be funny. That is what much of the voice acting is like in this game: Urkel.
Auto-save is highly flawed. Nuff said. Also don't choose the food-effect-doubling trait; that is broken (but still in the game for you to waste your precious points on). You can't pause the game, even with some quests and effects being timed. On the other hand, if you fail a timed quest because your phone rang, at least there is Auto-save. Oh, wait....

My male toon is a ranger, but looks more like a former pro wrestler who took radioactive steroids for many, many years. His arms and chest are so over-the-top that even his elbow is wider than my female's waist, and there is no option to adjust either. If Urkel had a dream where he was a huge hulking gladiator champion, this is what my *ranger* looks like! You think Arnold is big? Pffft! That's nothing, this is MUTANT URKEL,THE DESTROYER!!!!, light on his feet, and quick with a bow. :-/
Divinity gives you LOTS of text to read from NPCs. The writing is totally meh. Long paragraphs of text would be cool if they came from rich, engaging characters, but half of Divinity's writing is just redundant over-bloated schlock which I can't skip past because I might miss that one important tip. So I read it all. Meh. Meh. Meh. ...and yet more redundant over-bloated meh.
At level 2, I am offered the chance to join an organization and work my way up. I pass on that quest. Doesn't sound like the path I want to take. Turning down quests in this linear game (even just one) isn't a good idea, especially if you don't take the Talk With Animals trait, because apparently the animals offer quests in this game, but only to those who speak "Animal."
Still level 2, I'm given a mission (main storyline) to prevent
unless I
because, you know, that's just the kind of thing that only a level 2 hero could possibly set straight... just please pardon the water bucket I'm wearing on my head, it's just that I haven't been able to find a real helmet you see, but yeah, I'm The Chosen One, I guess. Why not? Even if that other organization wanted to start me out on the bottom rung just five minutes ago, I'm clearly the best choice to solve the biggest problem in the history of ever. Urkel (weaing an upside-down water bucket on his head) would be right at home in this travesty. Truly. Now imagine this painful scene overlayed with a somber classical piano score endlessly slogging into oblivion, and you start to see why I give this game a thumbs down rating. It desperately tries to be both silly and compellingly serious at the same time, but inspires only a certain longing to be in a dentist's chair, huffing nitrous oxide, forcing myself to think about Katy Perry while the sound of a drill drones on endlessly, and I stoically try to convince myself that my sweat is from the hot sun as Katy and I stroll down the beach, hand-in-hand, talking about penguins. I'd pay money to experience only one of these two ordeals again. I'll let you guess which one.
Crafting: are you really supposed to discover all on your own, that you can split a stack of hair and craft something by putting the stack back together? Hair + hair = thread. How are you supposed to ever figure that out on your own when the game automatically stacks duplicate items for you? I like games that don't hold my hand, but come on!! Why isn't that in the tutorial? Also, the crafting isn't rich and rewarding. Cook iron ore in the *food oven* (!) once, and it is an iron bar, twice and it becomes a steel bar?!! Steel shouldn't just be twice-baked iron. You should at least have to add a little lemon zest or something! And while I'm at it, in a game where hair is actually used in crafting, and where pie is craftable, why can't you craft hair pie? Come on! I guess we don't even give an indirect nod to adult humor in Urkel's House of Good Clean Fun.
Inventory: when you mouseover an item in your bag, a box pops up showing details. An *opaque* box. A big black unadjustable opaque box that blocks out the other items in your bag. When I'm looking for one specific item among 70, I like to use my cursor and let my eyes follow. Don't try that in this game; it makes you want to stick knitting needles through your nipples, twist them 12 times, then let go and run around the room pretending to be a turboprop airplane! Oh wait, you HAVE to do that in game, cuz that's how you craft: by dragging one item in your inventory on top of another item in your inventory. Hold it! Where's the second item? I can't see it cuz of that opaque info box!!  ARRRGGHHHH!!!! Where are my knitting needles?! (This WILL happen to you if you play this game, as surely as my name is Bullwinkle!)
At level 5, I entered The_Level_5_Dungeon (it's what you do). To progress to the second level, I needed to find a secret.  After about 10 minutes, I figured that I needed to do X. And in fact doing X does reveal the secret for most people, but either I had my camera pointing in the wrong direction, or too far zoomed in, or maybe I looked away from the monitor during the critical 0.8 seconds, because I never saw the secret get revealed. So for me, doing X seemed to have no effect, and you can't do X twice. Its not like pulling a lever that has 2 interchangeable positions; No, you can only do X once. So I just kept searching for the secret that allows you to progress down to the next level. No idea what it is, but I'll just keep searching for ... something, somehwere. It is so well hidden, it blends in so well, that I'm embarassed to tell you how long I kept searching before breaking down and going to the wiki. 2 HOURS! Unacceptable! Before reading: this review is about Beat Hazard Ultra, meaning the basic game + dlc. While I still recommend Beat Hazard on its own, it is more simplistic and lacks online co-op that the Ultra version provides, so I strongly recommend this game to be played with DLC.
Beat Hazard Ultra is a fast paced space shoot'em up with bright colorful graphics. At first sight it does not look like much, however it has several features that have made it one of the most pleasant surprises in my library.
The graphics look amazing at first, they tend to tire out your eyes pretty easily however, so it is not recommended to play for long sessions. There is an option to scale them up (!) or down inside the game menu though.The battle is fluid despite the abundance of color, enemies and the genral chaos that takes place on your screen especially on the higher difficulties. I have even played this on a linux netbook -yes it plays on linux and mac as well- with minimal capabilities and I was honestly surprised at its smoothness. Gameplay is fluid as well, regardless if you are playing with a controller or a mouse and keyboard. In fact, I even find myself preferring the mouse and keyboard mostly because the mouse provides more precise aiming than thumbsticks. The difficulty curve is just right, meaning you can choose from 5 different difficulty settings (easy, normal, hardcore, insane, suicidal) and play in whatever mode you feel comfortable with. This makes the game equally enjoyable for both hardcore shmup players as well as people who are new to the genre, or not particularly skilled. There is also a nice "perk" system implemented, where you can buy upgrades, such as a few special attacks, more multipliers, etc.
Music is an integral part of playing the game and your ship's power as well as enemies generated depend on the music you are playing. This means that the exact same level will be generated when you play the exact same track. When the music gets more aggressive, so will your ship's lasers, but that will also make your enemies spawn and move faster. The opposite happens when the music gets mellow. This makes the game quite interesting since it doesn't exactly mean it gets easier on mellow music or harder on heavier music, but instead it manages very successfully to keep the game balanced on either setting so you can have a go on different tracks depending on your mood. The games build in track list is fairly pleasant to play, but why limit yourself there, when you can actually index and play any song in your computer or just play listening to your favorite radio station?
What usually disappoints in this genre is the lack of online co-op mode. Well, Beat Hazard Ultra actually HAS online co-op as well as online versus mode where you can easily invite someone over your steam friend list and play together. You can even play listening to the radio, or play your own music as well, provided both of the participants have the same track indexed.
To sum it up, if you like shmups or are just curious about the genre, you will definitely enjoy this game. For me, it is a small gem in my library, so I hope more people will discover it in the future.

I so want to love this game, so much has been done right.  Unfortunately, many will not get beyond the first few hours of frustration as wave upon wave of monsters pummel, burn, freeze and feather your party with arrows.   You will reload again and again and then go online to read how many people have their favorite class and builds and strategies.  People recite obscure tips and how they love that the game doesn't hold your hand and how you are an idiot if you don't know where to go next. They all miss the point:  Larian simply couldn't or didn't bother to balance the front end of the game so it works.  A game should unfold organically and let you enjoy what it has to offer (this isn't necessarily "hand holding").  I'm ok with slow pace and difficult sections but in trying to avoid a linear "on rails" storyline they've simply placed brutal encounters everywhere around you that effectively gate the player in.  Many will find after a few hours they are essentially trapped in the starting town, unable to leave.
Graphics are good but not great.  Combat is very well done and ability to use objects and terrain (flammable liquids, water, etc.) is very interesting in the few moments you have before your group is slaughtered.   Inventory is terrible, and you will spend too much time figuring out what to equip to whom as upgrades/stats are hard to see and understand.  Quests are formulaic.  One day, someone will redo a goldbox game with much of what Larian has here and many will rejoice.  1/4 quests and 3/4 action.
I will keep trying to get further into this one but damn they've made it unnecessarily not fun at the outset.   Patch it Larian, just the first act, and you'll pick up so many more players.

Killing Floor 2 can be enjoyable in short bursts, especially if you're a new player. The classes are somewhat enjoyable, although some of their perks appear to be bugged. The maps hold some creativity to them, however, they also feel rather static. You can't jump across obstacles (Cars, railings and the like.) except for a couple of vehicles. I'm uncertain if they did this in order to prevent the AI from walking across absolutely everyting in order to reach you, but it's ruining my experience nonetheless. Yes, there are a few collectables that you can find if you enjoy exploration. The graphics are sufficable (although I expected more from the UE3 engine), the weapon designs decent. I enjoyed the re-skins they released for events such as Halloween and Christmas, but that's essentially it. I'm going to list a couple of annoying glitches and design decisions which ruined my experience entirely:
The game has a 50/50% chance to freeze your entire PC if you happen to Alt-Tab while it's loading. It happened to me several times and it was infuriating.
Odd graphical glitch with Destroyer of Worlds. Essentially, if you're playing Demo don't expect to see the entire map covered in Nukes. For some odd reason, you'll always end up seeing 1-2 mushroom clouds at best, while the rest of your team can see up to 7.
The god damn ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t greedy♥♥♥♥♥corporate Marketplace and reward system. Oh, what's that? You managed to get a crate or an USB after god knows how many matches? Congratulations! Now you only need to PURCHASE the key for.. how much was it? 2 euros? And no, the key isn't an actual rare drop. The only way to obtain it is to buy it with real money. And yes, I am aware of the golden crates which you can obtain by doing dailies. 1mil dosh for a crate, and each daily gives you about 50k. 3 dailies. Have fun grinding.
The annoying french♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who won't shut the ♥♥♥♥ up unless you mute the entire game, like I did.
The game feels exactly like its predecessor. In fact, it's a re-skin. Better graphics, but everything else feels exactly the same. A quick cash in. As much as I want to enjoy the game and see past its problems, I just can't do it. How this game has a Very Positive review is beyond me. There are numerous problems with it, most of which are fixable with an update or two. But even so, it's ungodly repetitive. And in case it wasn't obvious enough, I absolutely despise games in which you're stuck doing the same exact thing over and over again until the end of time, like Grindframe and Vermintide.
No, Killing Floor 2 is not a colossal failure. It can be fun, especially during the Weeklys and on harder difficulties. My friend and I had a lot of fun playing the most recent Weekly challenge. The game has potential, but the flaws I stated previously are simply holding it back too much, at least for players like me who expect a system which actually rewards you instead of encouraging you to spend RL money in order to get a worthwhile item. That, in addition with the mind numbingly repetitiveness in gameplay is effectively preventing me from actually acknowledging the positives the game has to offer.

Lethal League (LL) is the quintessence of competitive arcade gameplay. Being completely free of over complication, Team Reptile have fortunately channelled the most special elements of the nostalgic games of the golden era, where a sole focus on gameplay has driven design and development. The result being a game with no apparent story, not character progression, and no cheap ways of making you feel as though you should be playing the game, instead it slaps you in the face with a fresh take on Fighters, that is plain and simply, unsullied fun.
The gameplay and structure of LL lends itself perfectly to the resolution of longstanding disagreements (1-on-1 Fights), bouts of personal worth and glory (4 way FFA), and also to bond-building exercises (2-on-2 Team Fights). The beautiful thing about the simple gameplay is it works so well not only in the hectic 4-way FFA, but also in 1-on-1 combat, where the simple mechanics eventually boil down to a game of whits, where you are more trying to force the other player/s to swing at the wrong point, or you are trying to think and act fast enough to catch them off-guard.
That long winded jargon can be distilled down to; this game is perfect for playing with friends, and that is exactly how it should be consumed. This game has one of those qualities where if you get served too hard, you will hate it; so take it in with friends and you will instantly see the gratifying outcome of learning together, while also pulling off some badass manoeuvres resulting in you all squealing like manly Girl Scouts. We have not tried it in Online Play as my internet services would make the game run like an interactive slideshow. But we can safely say that by grabbing a few ales, a few controllers, and huddling around your PC, you will be parting in the finest display of competition I have seen in a video games since Mario Party 64.
Team Reptile have not given this game a huge amount of content, with 5 characters and 6 Levels, BUT, the content in the game is so perfectly polished, I question whether the development team is really as small as they say. We would love to see more playable characters and levels in the future just to give the game that bit of spice, but where it stands now is a testament to where AAA game development falls short in modern game development; where such heavy focus on being the next money making machine makes games lose that…specialness.
From a developer’s standpoint this game has soul, you can feel the love that went into it when you play it. So get it, you won’t be disappointed.
3 / 3 Worth Playing

I eye my top-heavy crocodile opponent from across the field as a purple coated ball begins to spawn between us. He points his stout towards the object, knowing that he's going to smash this into my cold, yellow face. Not today, Latch. Not today.
The ball materializes and we rush towards it. My cane is already extended for an over the head smash to hit the reptilian foe below me. Time seems to stop as I connect with the latent power resting within the ball. The crocodile was quick to react and seemed to stop all momentum I had with my initial hit with one tap of his nose. The ball soared over me, and before I connected with the ground the crocodile was already rallying the ball against a wall, hoping to power up another devastating blow.
I rush to intervene in his sadistic wall-ball ritual, tapping the ball out of his rhythm at an upwards angle. Furious, Latch's eyes glowed red towards the cane that brought an end to his games. He claws the wall in front of him and begins to climb up its structure to catch up to the ball. Flipping outwards, he catches the ball in his mouth and my world goes dark. All I can see is the crocodile's burning descent from the wall, his eyes reflecting my helpless yellow face.
I jump upwards to dodge the assult, but Latch releases the saliva-covered ball angled with precision towards my jump peak. The counter at the bottom reads into the hundreds, and I know that reflecting this is going to take all the luck in my thin smiley-faced bones. My cane relexively reaches in defense, and this was all the luck I needed. The ball's momentum is reversed right at the crocodile's pointed nose. But what stops him from doing exactly what I just did?
I try to land a second hit and throw Latch off his prediction. He sees this and attempts to outsmart my own moves. We negate each other's attacks with a twang of cane and stout, the ball landing just behind Latch. I see it bounce off the corners of the rotting arena with bliding speed, and I process that it's coming right back at me. Cane out, I bunt the ball directly downwards into where the crocodile attempts another intervention. His tail whips around, but he is too early.
The ball lightly bounces off the top of his scaly skull, and he's sent below the arena.
BURST 2, BEGIN!

Saints Row IV is a sandbox experience like no other. It's hard to believe how much the series has changed but you know what?
I think it's for the better.
Saints Row 2 was pretty great, but it felt too much like a typical GTA clone, yeah it had some crazy stuff but for the most part it was just another generic sandbox game,with little to differentiate it from other games like it on the market.  I haven't played it in a while and sadly I don't remember it too much, but it was a lot of fun, if unoriginal.
Then came Saints Row:The Third, and while it was an fairly enjoyable experience, it made some poor decisions like having a pointless choice system or killing off the best character in the series 20 minutes in.
It had a fairly boring city in Steelport, which was a completely lifeless and stale open world in comparison to Stillwater from 2. The game was also quite short, with it also having a few terrible missions(the zombie mission in particular was dreadful), and having a LOT of really juvenile humour.
As for the new characters, I really enjoyed Oleg, he had some great dialogue and was a cool ally to have. Angel was pretty cool too, what with his backstory with Killbane and everything, he was an interesting character.
Overall it was fun, however, it was a bit disappointing in comparison to the second one.
Finally we have the most recent installment, last year's Saints Row IV, and it's probably the best game in the franchise so far I think.
For one, this game starts off with a bang, as Cyrus Temple(one of the main antagonists of Saints Row The Third) has went from leader of military group STAG, to becoming a full blown terrorist(when people said this game was ridiculous, THEY WEREN'T LYING), and you, Pierce, Shaundi, and newcomer Asha Odekar along with transmissions from Kinzie and bad guy turned good Matt Miller have to infiltrate his base in an unknown foreign country to stop him.
After your character takes down Cyrus, you'll start climbing a rocket to the sound of Aerosmith's 1998 classic, "I Don't Wanna Miss A Thing". Everyone starts saying their goodbyes as you climb the rocket to sacrifice yourself for the good of the planet...although after attaching the bomb to the rocket you jump off and give a thumbs up once the rocket explodes behind you, and then you land in the chair of...THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA?!?!?!? And after all that, only then does the game's logo show up for the first time...BEST OPENING FOR A GAME EVER
The game takes place in Steelport...BUT NOT AS WE KNOW IT. It is a simulation of Steelport as an alien leader named Zinyak has invaded Earth and has abducted you and your crew, and now you have to find a way out of the simulation, save your friends, and stop the evil Zin empire.
The main reason this game succeeds where Saints Row The Third didn't, is that though the plot is ridiculous, it never gets in the way. That zombie mission from 3 felt like filler and it interrupted the flow of the game, along with a few others that dragged, Saints Row IV's missions on the other hand always feel fresh,interesting, and of course, FUN! In one mission, you're gunning down alien ships one by one as the president of the USA, the next you're saving a comrade by flying in to save him in a giant power armor suit, in another you're beating up a giant Saints Flow can named Paul as a statue, and in another you're playing in a Streets of Rage p**stake called Saints of Rage! The variety is definitely welcome.
The superpowers make the game SO MUCH FUN. Running incredibly fast, jumping insanely high, running up walls, gliding and more are just some of the cool powers you can receive. For taking down enemies you can freeze them, set them on fire, throw them with telekinesis and stomp the ground to create shock waves that send enemies flying! It's all insanely cool.
The humour is excellent here as well, with tons of great lines and references, and an incredibly funny parody of the romance system in Mass Effect, helped by the fantastic delivery from the voice actors, including Keith David playing himself, Nolan North as one of the voices for the president,Daniel Dae Kim as Johnny Gat and Terry Crews replaces the late Michael Clarke Duncan as Benjamin King, and he does a fantastic job. The voice work overall is great all around.
The soundtrack is also a MAJOR improvement over 3, tons of fantastic music here like some great dubstep like Blow The Roof by Flux Pavillion or Vindicate by Excision & Datsik, What is Love by Haddaway, Don't Wanna Miss A Thing by Aerosmith, Song 2 by Blur, and more!
The graphics are relatively unchanged from 3, though cutscenes look slightly better now I think, and the textures also seems to be a little sharper than 3.
The customization is fantastic, and is much better than 3's, though sadly cars are rendered completely pointless because of your superpowers(who wants to drive a car when you can run up buildings or glide instead?).
Weapons have TONS of upgrades and there are also so many different weapons it will take you ages to upgrade each and every one! From the dubstep gun to the abduction gun, to the the golf club to the tentacle bat(I think I know where this is going!), there's tons of variety on display here.
While the map is still Steelport, it has been tweaked and ultimately it does feel different to Steelport in SR 3, and this game has much better activities too, like the ridiculously fun Insurance Fraud now has superpowers, which honestly makes it even more fun than it already was, the return of Fight Club in Super Powered Fight Club,which is an incredibly fun battle arena mode where you can kill tons of Zin with your superpowers and you'll see many familiar faces from previous games, and an activity where you can destroy everything in the power armor suit. Overall, the activities are great fun in this game.
Side missions are also available for all the characters, and all characters have a fun little mission called a loyalty mission where at the end the character in that mission turns into a super powered version of themselves, and you can use them as a homie later on in the sandbox, and finishing all of them gives you the best ending(there's two endings).
The game is quite long too, main story is about 10-12 hours, with TONS to do after finishing the game and you could easily play it for 40-50 hours, and even more with Co-Op and DLC!
Overall, Saints Row IV is an incredibly enjoyable game, I can easily recommend it to anyone who was disappointed with SR 3, as there are tons of great references to the first and second games.
With fantastic humour, memorable characters, awesome superpowers, great voice work, fun and inventive scenarios, and an awesome soundtrack, Saints Row IV is an incredible game.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is my first game of the series. I saw this game from a review by Totalbiscuit and had to pick it up. While the bugs have frustrated me occasionally, the experience watching my own squad essentially kill themselves from panic was worth it. I've gone through pain and misery watching 95% shots fail, and being ambushed by what felt to be an infinite amount of aliens pouring through the fog of war. Needless to say, I can't want for November 2015 when Firaxis releases XCOM 2.
The strategy behind this game goes in depth significantly. There are, to me, two stages of the game. One is managing your base and resources to work with, whether that be weapon development, buildings, and panic of countries. Focusing your resources to one area leaves the others weak, meaning UFOs can win in aerial battles, countries may panic more easily, or your soldiers may find themselves weak on weaponry in the battlefield. For many of the people here who want to hit 100% perfection on XCOM, good luck. This game is all about cutting your losses in the higher difficulties, and staying alive rather than going big for rewards.
Newcomers to XCOM, as well as veterans from the older games can come try this game out. It offers a skill cap that punishes mistakes quite hard, but not enough to discourage a newbie to keep pressing on. Being on your toes with strategy, movement, and the future of the XCOM project make the game very rewarding with one downside. Sometimes a plan won't go correctly, and you'll delude yourself into thinking the game is against you. The reality of XCOM is that you never had the odds on your side. The aliens have stronger weaponry and many times more numbers than you would ever have. To the newcomers of XCOM, I'd strongly recommend against downloading the acclaimed Long War mod, as it is massively more punishing in comparison to the vanilla game.
The amount of content in this game is insane. Without the Enemy Within DLC or the free Long War mod, the game can last over 100 hours on a single campaign run. Adding those two can bring the game to triple the length. Both these two additions bring increased depth to everything, from new weapon types and genetic/mech modifications to your soldiers. For Enemy Within, a third force that seeks to side with the aliens is also against you, and their purpose is to mess with you as hard as possible, draining your resources if left unchecked. Long War increases the difficulty up a notch by increasing the health of the aliens, as well as their numbers. I'd strongly recommend playing it on normal difficulty even if you have beaten the vanilla game on a higher difficulty.
Overall XCOM Enemy Unknown is a great experience to have. You build bonds with your squad, and can customize them to how you like them. Watching them grow and conquer aliens is amazingly fun, even if you have already beaten the game once or twice. The feeling of progression outside combat transitions to inside, with your soldiers adorning your dedication to researching new armors, weapons, and enhancements. The countries that contribute to XCOM's monthly budget reward your continued success with more resources, allowing you to proceed faster. All of this can go backwards as well, making XCOM an engaging challenge that any strategic gamer should take.

I honestly don't remember why I bought this game besides the fact that I was looking for a different kind of rpg.  Something that wasn't the generic turn based game.  I found one despite being girlish and sexualized at points, the game contains a lot of humerous references from a lot of other games.  The story is lengthy and it has a lot to read but its very entertaining.
The gameplay is very broad, there is so much stuff to do and it all requires some grinding.  You don't just randomly find item drops you find "plans" which you then need materials to craft the item the plan is for.  But plans aren't only for weapons and items, you can actually change the way the game plays.  Gain more exp, complete a plan for a whole new character, a new dungeon, mod the dungeon to have different monsters and literally so much more.
The combat looked interesting but it turns bland once you figure out the best way to deal damage.
There are 3 kinds of attacks, all of which will fill the exe gauge and deal damage to the targets and their guard.
-Rush combos will increase the amount exe gauge from attacking which is used for special skills
-power combos hit for more damage
-break combos do more damage to their guard bar
At first break combos seem to be the smart thing to use as once their guard is down they take more damage.  But by the time their guard is down they're just about dead.  The only time this seems to work is when you're against a big boss that has a lot of health.  Brute forcing with pure damage is just faster and better, some bosses have more guard bar than they do health.  With buffs and points in the exe gauge its easy to deal a lot of damage once you've found a good set up for your team.  Late game you'll be using only rush combos and exe skills.

I have no idea why I like this game so much. It's super girly, too colourful, and the dialogue that TRIES to be funny is annoying.
I guess I'm just really in love with the battle system. It feels rewarding to learn new moves for each character and add them to your combo strings. I love RPG's that give you the option to have more than just one basic attack during battle. In each combo string, you have three choices: 1) Guard Break 2) Rush and 3) Power Attack. Your goal is to break down the guard of your enemies so that your power attacks have more...well...POWER! However, if you choose to use Rush attacks, it can work towards building your EXE bars.
EXE bars give you the opportunity to have a 5th attack in your combo string, and there's 4 different levels. The more EXE bars you have filled up, the higher level EXE attacks you can use. EXE Skills on the other hand are also beautifully animated super attacks, kinda like Limit Breaks from Final Fantasy, that you can use to dish out a ton of damage. They are lot of fun to unlock, as well as use once you've broken down the enemy's guard.
The story of Hyperdimension Neptunia is nothing really special. Apparently all the Goddesses and CPU's are supposed to represent current gen consoles like XBOX360, PS3 and Wii-U. The main character Neptune I think is supposed to represent you, the player, trying to find a way to mend the bad blood between them all and have them unite the land of Gameindustri.
The dialogue in this game can sometimes get annoying with absolutely no direction in the story line. I really LOVE the parts where actual conflict occurs and moves the story forward, and although it's a basic plot of uniting nation leaders through combat against a common foe, I actually enjoy it. Which is weird since I normally look for something deeper in storylines like something akin to Life is Strange where they tackle the social issues youth face on a daily basis.
Want a deep storyline? Ain't gonna find it here. Want a lot of useless dialogue that tries to be cute, funny, and cheeky? You got RIGHT HERE and I hate it. Yet this is the game I've played the most in my entire Steam library? Why? The battle system is awesome, and so is the PLAN system, where you can hunt and gather various items in order to unlock a variety of things: extra dungeons, extra enemies per dungeon, new item harvest per dungeon, other aid items, weapons etc etc etc the list goes on.
Despite of my deep deep hatred for the pointless dialogues about every character's favourite pudding and their desire for more pudding--I have thoroughly enjoyed this game for its character customization options.

It's been some time since I read it, but this is a very good visual novel. The quality of the endings varies a bit, but some are really good. The best written ending I encountered is actually one of the bad endings.
If you are a parent I advice you to check this "game" (visual novel) out before you let a kid read it through, and that you check all the endings out. Some are very emotional, and some are very grim. The endings are often also well done, and in much they are often a strength of this visual novel. I do however feel that the disclaimer in the beginning is very valid, after reading all endings through. (I do not want to get into more details to avoid spoilers, but I'm talking about
) The environments the story takes place in are bright and colorful, but at times stuff can get grim and the setting can change.
The main character, Semyon, lives in what is more or less the world some years ago. He has a wierd dream that he has had repeatedly, that's how it all starts. Then you are introduced to the guy, who is supposed to be a rather misserable guy that hasn't really achieved anything in life. (Although, there are some things he did achieve that I never did, even so... O.o) He is usually sitting at home in front of his computer, with few interactions with the "real" world. He gets a message from someone he kept in contact with since university, and he is convinced to go to a party with the people he studied with. He goes down to take the bus... And while on the bus he falls asleep. As he wakes up it's summer, not winter as when he fell asleep, and the bus is out in "nowhere" instead of the city where he was previously. This is really where the story begin, and he begins with freaking out a bit. Then he enters the nearby camp where he meets different characters that he interacts with (mainly girls). He is now forced to partake in the activities of the summer camp, meanwhile trying to figure out what's going on. He also has the options of falling in love with a girl (which girl depends on the choices made at key points throughout the story) or to not fall in love. Most but not all girls have a good and a bad ending depending on if you make them love Semyon or not. It's not always obvious what choice will lead to what, improving the story since you likely don't always know if you will get a good or bad ending until it happens.
I really like this visual novel, and I would recommend it to anyone searching for a good story.
Also, if you only played it through once and thought the ending was bad, please give it one or two more tries, since the endings are different and you may think some endings are weaker than others. (Like Alisa's endings, they were too similar wheter it was the good or bad ending and it felt they could be improved; there was even a new ending made by the developer as a mod to get another ending, although it's in russian, but it was translated into english by someone and should be available if you search a bit.)
This is a "free to play" visual novel that may make you wish you had paid money for it due to the quality it delivers.
So, in short, a good visual novel well worth your time.

Banner Saga is beautifully drawn and written. The strength of the art quickly draws you into an engrossing drama. Unlike many games, Banner saga doesn't pull you in with addictive gameplay mechanics. Instead, the game feels like a great novel that you can't put down til the end. The tactical combat is interesting enough, but this facet of the game is easily overshadowed by the interesting and challenging choices you are asked to make as the narrative progresses.
If you enjoy story-driven games and/or a good fantasy novel, Banner Saga is a must play. If you're a hardcore fan of tactics games, Banner Saga doesn't break any new ground there. What it does is showcase the possibilities when you let narrative steal the show and put gameplay in a supporting role.

This is a tragic failure to do gameplay testing. An incredible game, with utterly arbitrary expectations for play style. I went from loving every minute for the first six hours, to hating every minute for the next six. I don't know if I have the stamina to reroll everything to cater to the developer's poorly communicated requirements to enjoy the later content. I simply used an online guide to plan a party full of wizards, and suddenly the game was so easy I could progress much farther. Unfortunately, poor quest design and lopsided mechanics made it essential to continually look up mechanicaly subsystems, fiddly quest triggers and nuances of crafting. This is a game I loved, then hated, and now find to be merely average. It could have been a great, spontaneous romp of joy.
