I'm going to start off by saying that the Spec Requirements needs to be updated severely. In the description (which not a lot of people read) it lists a Quad Core i5 or i7 while the Spec Requirements only list ANY Dual Core. This is a significant difference.
From what I can tell, this is not supposed to "impact" gaming by utilizing the CPU rather than GPU. On my system, it maxed out the CPU (all 8 cores) and caused significant frame drop upon recording a light-weight game. GPU utlization never toppled over 40% and that was just a one-time spike, average was 26%. Meanwhile, Xsplit uses 26% CPU and 21% GPU as average.
During recording, both microphone, and game audio became desynched by as little as 5 seconds but with lengthier videos, it was 20 seconds.
The settings for recording where a bit lacking but very good for such a light-weight program.
The UI is very nice, both for Game recorder and Screen recorder.
All-in-all, this program has great potential but needs a lot of core work to utilize the CPU better.

It is difficult to be critical of something which is free but I feel like after sinking 8 hours into this, I need to at least share my opinion. I don't feel like this review contains spoilers but if you're extremely sensitive about that sort of thing, you might want to stop reading this now.
The story meanders very slowly for about the first third and eventually gets more interesting and picks up the pace for the middle third. The final third gave the impression that things were wrapping up but all I got was a cliché ending and no questions were answered. After the ending I got, I reloaded the last autosave to make a different choice and get a different ending but both were equally unsatisfactory. I wish I had known that this was one of those stories that keeps you wondering at the end, rather than explicitly explaining everything.
On a slightly separate frustrating issue, it felt like the story involved building quite a few different relationships, and some of those might veer in certain directions as a result of choices you make along the way. However, the hinted intentions never became anything and I was left wondering why the choices I made seemingly had no effect on my relationship with particular people.
Although my review is critical and sounds fairly negative, I would still recommend giving this a playthrough because the story was *just* compelling enough to keep my attention to the end and it cost me nothing to experience.
edit: I forgot to mention that some parts of the game were uncharacteristically salacious and didn't feel in keeping with the theme or story. I wasn't offended by it but it just felt out of place and quite ridiculous.

I, being a late-comer to gaming and Battlefront 2 being one of the earlier console games I played (along with GUN and I believe Flatout), can quickly say that this game is gorgeous and sold the industry to me.
It's massive, it's immersive, it's quick-to-play, and it's
Who doesn't like Star Wars? Well, plenty of people, but... hey, you can't dislike the adorable Stormtroopers.
You've got all the stuff other shooting games do. Guns, people to shoot guns, and some extra things like vehicles. Then there's the space battles, which make an entirely different challenge and one of the most glorious flying experiences in gaming, and then you've got the tactical 'Conquest' part where you put around a giant fleet of spacecraft for your favorite faction in the Star Wars movies.
Rebels, Empire/Republic, CIS: You can play as any of them, which is great fun. Each have their own soldiers and classes, allowing different experiences for every team. It's especially cool to roll around as a droideka, then unfurl and be destroyed by a Jedi. At least you're the envy of your friends.
The battles themselves are manic and titanic. Hoth a devoid planet? Not when you're in the middle of a 100+ person skirmish between Rebels and Imperials. AT-AT action is amazing, until you're taken down by some jerk in a cheap snowspeeder. Maybe it was SKYWALKER?
No.
There's also that option to play as a Jedi or Sith or melodramatic bounty hunter popping up every now-and-then, but they're lame and die too quickly. I don't suggest them. Well, MBH is alright, but who wants to get eaten by a sandpit monster?
There's the few issues, like absurdly dumb AI and logical errors (downwards gravity in space?), but they're far and few compared to the joy this game brings.
I couldn't recommend this enough. And it's only 10 bucks USD!

A twin-stick shooter, mixed with an Audiosurf-style music engine, mixed with a dance party. Beat Hazard is a flashy, spectacular, intense game that looks glorious on your big-screen TV... unless you're epileptic. Its built-in soundtrack is a groovy electronica mix of various indie artists and styles, but in Beat Hazard you can never complain about the crap music, since it hooks in to your own music library.
As a twin-stick shooter it's more style than substance. The controls are decent, your weapons range from tiny lasers to huge lasers (depending on the intensity of your music at any given time), and there's a range of enemies. But it's not the game you play when you want a twin-stick shooter.
It's great when you set it on "Easy", put on some music you like, get a drink, treat it as a WinAmp visualiser, and chillax the heck out.

Very awesome fighting game.
It's a cross-over fighting game, but I was able to enjoy it with no knowledge of most characters when I first started.
It's an anime fighter, as one could tell from the anime artstyle.  Thus, you will encounter some mechanics from similar games such as air-dashes, a focus on long and flashy combos, burst and roman cancel systems, etc.
Like other fighters of this subgenre, normals are split into three buttons: A, B, and C, representing Light, Medium, and Heavy attacks.  This game also include additional buttons D and E for even slower and stronger normals, as well as a universal dash-cancelling system.
The game has a visual novel styled story mode.  The roles of the characters are presented such that knowledge of their original source isn't needed too much.
The sound effects are decent, and the music is pretty dang awesome.  Every character has their own theme that plays during fights.  You will generally hear the theme for player 2's character, like it or not.
Command buffering is VERY lenient.  I'd honestly say this is one of the easiest fighting games to get into thanks to the buffer, as it helps to learn basic combos when you first start out.  That said, there's still a lot of depth with its various systems such as the dash cancelling and assist systems.
Unfortuantely, the AI is mostly a joke.  I can easily breeze through fights against them without much problem.
As per usual fighting game tradition, the final boss of arcade mode is a cheater.  One can easily dominate against the last boss with proper knowledge of their character and the game mechanics, but making a single mistake can be very punishing.
Online is unfortunately not that active, but one can set up matches within the community discord.
My only gripe with this game is that the keyboard remapping could be improved.  P1 is locked into using WASD and P2 is locked into using the arrow keys for movement.  There's no way to switch them.  Additionally, P2 cannot remap their buttons to any of the WASD keys, so if you're used to using those keys.  You will need to use an external program to use them for attacks..

At first sight not a very exciting story, but getting more and more interesting: The protagonist Semyon is just an ordinary guy living in a big city.
But suddenly he falls asleep in a bus in winter waking up in a pioneer camp in summer... wait what just happened?!
Spending time in a pioneer camp out of nowhere, meeting new people (indeed girls), exploring places and trying to get out of there... or staying there?
At this point you should expect a lot of monologue and dialogue (like in every visual novel i guess), but it's not getting boring don't worry!
Well.... first of all: I loved that game. Even it has its "negative sides" (I don't even know if you can call them so) IT'S FREE! Im very grateful, that I could play it for free.
So let's go ahead.
What I love about this game?
It's weird because its kinda an eroge game (indeed it is lol) but I didn't rly care tbh because I just wanted to play a good visual novel with or without romantic sides. Who think it's just a 0815 dating-simulator, well.. It's not. It's something more than that.
The delevopers put a lot of effort and love in this game, I don't even know. The MOST stunning thing for me was truly the backgrounds of this game... you can just lean back and enjoy them.
Overall the arts were great, sure details of the characters changed from time to time (for instance: Alisa's hair colour changing from brown to blond etc.) and many CG's were nearly the same except the characters.
But still: every route had its details and another outcome. That was quite a "experience" for me.
I thought a lot about this game. To understand the characters, why they do that and so on.
What this game really is about. How important are the decisions I do in my life?
Moreover, I rly liked and enjoyed every character.
There is lots to do: many decisions, many routes, good and bad endings + some extra content to dive deeper in the story. I did every route except the bad endings. For me they were all worth it the time and you should really take some time to think about this game and enjoy it of course.
BTW I loved the humor! Yeah maybe not everyone watches anime or reads manga.. but there were several references. Just take one moment for a closer look :P Don't worry it's not full of them, the comments from our protagonist are pretty funny too.
What sometimes a little annoyed me were the sudden russian translations.. but mistakes like that can happen a lot in a game. Sure I couldn't understand some sentences but Im fine with it.
Whatever..
Well why are you still reading this? Just play it already! I recommend it completely :)
I hope I didn't say too much, enjoy the game and I hope I could help you.

This game is truly awesome. Atmosphere Atmosphere Atmosphere ! ! !  It really feels like the armageddon hath cometh. It has all the awesome freedom of Diablo II to choose your stats and which skills to level/improve.  It has all the fast pacing, loot, and "seal chest" challenges of Diablo III. As a veteran of the Diablo series, I would hands down say that this game really continues the feel of Diablo II with its graphics and gameplay.
The huge draw is the option to dual-class at level 10.  This really unlocks so many different ways to play your character and allows for so much freedom. I enjoyed the necromancer, druid, and witch doctor of the Diablo series; thus, I created an occultist/shaman both of which can summon familiars.  D2 was a masterpiece and D3, while it has its drawbacks was a very fun game.  I would wholeheartedly recommend Grim Dawn as it is a masterpiece in its own right for blending D2/D3 and adding its own flavors and quirks.
Pros: many many quests, lots of loot, everything can be upgraded, and DUAL-CLASS!
Cons: some ally AI can get lost, but they teleport when too far; the multilevel areas can be hard to see as the transparency of the level can be off.
Final thoughts:  Great Game, buy it.

Players can buy upgrades with gold and upgrade their monsters with wrath.
Upgrading monsters and unlocking new gods to serve are the most fun aspects of crawl. However the gameplay gets tedious fast. With your player and three other ghosts on the screen at the same time all trying to do their own thing, it is VERY easy to lose track of what you can interact with and hard to explore environments. Crawl is too fast paced with players  moving from room to room with little time to properly react.
The controls are simple and not very inntuitive. The developers should have taken advantage of some other available buttons to add much needed variety. Crawl is a very good idea but needs a much bigger developer in order to get to the fantastic potential it has. Crawl should have been designed around an online multiplayer aspect with chat features in order to get the most out of it. If a developer would to take many of the main concepts of Crawl and couple it with online multiplayer then this would be an instant classic party game. As it stands now Crawl will never be much more than it already is, a party game not aimed at casuals with way too much going on at one time while being surprisingly lacking of content.
Great if you can pick it up extreamly cheap or have three or four other dedicated friends to play with, but very overpriced.

This game is amazing.  But I'm going to give you my opinion on the "P2W" System. And the Value of this game.
The "P2W" features are Pets, Cosmetics, Inventory Space, and Weight Limit.
PETS: The Pets will loot for you on a small cooldown (4-10 seconds). Can Use up to 4 at a time. Greatly speeds up grinding.
Alot of games do this now or add in a a loot radius feature. This game doesn't have a subscription so they opted for the pet method.  Also these can be bought in game for silver. Rather cheaply even..just pretty rare to come across.
COSMETICS: The Cosmetics do "help" in game a bit. For example, all Underwear adds +1 Luck.  The outfits that people seem to complain about being P2W however They hide your name. (How OP!! /sarcasm)
INVENTORY SPACE: You Can have a total of 192 slots of inventory space.  You get some spaces for free while you are lvling and questing. You can buy 1,4,8, or 16 more slots through the CS. Now, you think this is bad but once you get all the spaces thats all you ever pay for it. and its 192 SLOTS I can think of plenty of larger MMO's that dont let you have half of that.
WEIGHT LIMIT: Every item In BDO has weight (mostly). This is another thing you can buy and have forever. And yes it will help you while grinding. This combined with the Inventory Space will minimize your need to return to town to sell your spoils.
Now that we have Covered all the "issues" Lets go over how much all this will cost you should you decide you want it.
(Note: you can still play just fine w/o any of it. All they are is QoL features really.)
Base Game: $9.99 USD
Pets: 11.00 each lets say you buy 4  so $44.00 USD
Cosmetics: The " P2W" PvP costume Costs $34.00. The Underwear costs $7.00 USD
Inventory Space:  For this are just gonna do the +16 Inventory Expansion you would need about 10 of these to max out
they cost $14.50 USD Each so about $145.00 USD
Weight Limit: You can buy 200 LT, 150 LT, 100 LT, and 50 LT Coupons. You can use each of these only once per character for a Total of 500 more LT. Assuming you buy all of these they will cost you  $46.00 USD
Ok, So what we have here is a total cost of all the "P2W" that is deemed "Nessesary" and the game itself.
Which totals to:  $289.99 USD
Sounds like alot right? But heres the thing.
1. You need none of this stuff. and
2. WoW has cost me about $1400.00 USD ($420.00 just for the game.) and that isnt including Pets, Mounts, ETC.. And I still don't have  192 Slots of Inventory.
And that cost you can pay for it over time.... 10 bucks here and there wont be missed even by the poorest of people.

BUT That is your choice. You don't need to give your weapons special stats and additions to annihilate everything. The freerunning is awesome and pretty much lets you do anything and go anywhere. Then when the sun sets, the game changes. I won't say how but I wouldn't recommend casually walking the streets after 21:00.
I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who likes the excitement and thrill of being in danger basically everywhere.  As a final note... Goodnight, and Good luck.

+Beautiful
+Reliably and significantly updated
+Co-op/Teamwork orientated gameplay
+High skill ceiling
+Cosmetics system
-Repetitive gameplay
-Perks imbalanced
-Some weapons potentially obsolete
-Hard learning curve from easy to harder difficulties
Enemies have recognisable designs and movesets, making for clean understanding of gameplay and interesting decision making as the zeds (zombie enemies) learn more attacks and movements as the game difficulty increases. The guns are true to their real-life counterparts, Tripwire have done their best to motion capture everything for each weapon from their recoil, noise and bullet ejections to differing reload animations depending on how fast your character can reload in-game. All of this really shines when the game goes into slow motion (zed time) and you can appreciate everything's combined effect. And if that wasn't enough you've got the gore system that lets you rip apart the zeds any way you see fit.
The passion they have for their games is pretty evident with the aforementioned beauty and attention to details but they also have a proven track record for updating their games for many many years - Killing Floor 1, a mere mod at its base, was continually and consistently
and all through positive involvement with the KF community.
Updates for KF2 have so far involved new maps, perks, zeds, bosses, gamemodes, weapons, gameplay mechanics, and increasing access to cosmetics. I expect this game to only improve.
To level all perks to maximum you're looking at around 300 hours with the current 10 available perks.
The types of enemies that you face are limited even on the hardest difficulties and despite their movesets changing; perks share similar playstyles, such as gunslinger and sharpshooter both requiring headshots, or gunslinger and berserker both utilising movement speed to kite enemies (favouring less teamwork); and maps tend to have limited viable defence points especially for harder difficulties, so you'll find yourself in the same place quite often and even more so if you're using a perk that likes to remain stationary and/or keep its distance from zeds (sharpshooter/demolitionist).
For me, and despite the game's repetitive nature, the combat is satisfying and I still enjoy trying to maximise my effectiveness on each perk/map and adapting to the playstyles of my random teammates.
Luckily, the future looks bright - an
has been hinted for an upcoming update, giving people who don't see the challenge in the current max 10 wave system a reason to get excited.
For newer players, this won't be much of an issue, although, to the annoyance of long term players, new players are often finding themselves at suicidal and hell on earth accidentally or through chasing DOSH challenges, unaware of much of the information required to thrive. However, as people progress to harder difficulties game knowledge becomes key and certain perks outshine others.
Some perks are incredibly strong when it comes to surviving without teamwork and that largely comes down to healing and movement speed (e.g. the berserker has both with damage resistances and infinite ammo to boot). The general rule of thumb is if you can outrun the zed, you'll eventually beat it.
At the highest difficulties this imbalance truly rears its ugly head. A large problem is that if a class can't survive against a fleshpound/scrake or boss by itself then it becomes highly reliant on teamwork to kill the zed faster, or survive its attacks before you kill it. And thus, certain tactics or perks are favoured at higher levels of difficulty to survive waves rather than maintaining high levels of teamwork. Admittedly, the harder difficulties favour teamwork in some aspects. For example, sharing of dosh to the medic for the medic assault rife at early waves is optimum. Sadly, however, solo tactics are promoted even more when less experienced players are introduced because it makes relying on teamwork even worse.
But this isn't the fault of newer players. Information is kept from them, such as resistances of each zed to each damage type (e.g. fleshpounds are weak to explosives while scrakes are resistant to them), enemy movesets (e.g. husks gain a flamethrower attack at suicidal) and movements (crawlers will predict and dodge projectiles at harder difficulties) and much more -
With more bosses being added, it should make certain perks more viable as tactics have to adapt to suit the weaknesses of each boss. However, currently, perks that can outrun or outsustain the boss still stand a much higher chance of winning.
It should also be noted that ultimately some weapons are just better than others, and you end up buying the same weapons and in the same order every game, provided you don't get desperate or whatnot given a lack of dosh after dying.
The game has strong positives that everyone can appreciate, but negatives that are intolerable for many and seemingly tolerable to the few, including myself. I think I can recommend this game because I still get enjoyment out of it, despite the flaws I've pointed out. Perhaps it's because I've been with the game since KF1 and appreciate the improvements so much that I ignore the negatives, but regardless the game improves so consistently it seems like these issues can be solved in the forseeable future.

Child of Light is one of the best recent rpg's I have played.  When I first thought about playing this game I had decided that I would rather watch it on youtube, which would have turned out to be a huge mistake.  Since it's an rpg you get a lot more choice in how you play over somebody elses experience.
I think the story of this game is pretty good but not amazing, as it's told in a fairy tale type manner.  Every character speaks in rhyme, so a lot of the time they have to select words and phrases that would rhyme with the last, instead of telling a rich story.  But that isn't to say there is no story because there definetely is.  The main character actually grows up throughout the story, like she starts off selfish but becomes selfless to the end, unfortunately thats it for character growth though, at the end of the day everybody is there for the main character.
The combat of this game is 99% of the team easy and excellent, and if you play the game on casual mode you won't have to fight half the enemies in the game, it's really easy.  It's only on expert that the game becomes a lot harder.  It's a turn based rpg where your character moves across on a bar at the bottom, which depends on your speed stat.  Your character will start at the wait part of the bar, which is basically waiting to select a skill.  Once you hit the end of wait you will hit a line where you can select a skill.  Each skill has a time that it takes to get off, depending on it's strength.  Now the mechanic of the combat that makes it somewhat strategic, is the fact that if the enemy hits you well you are in the red bar you will get interrupted, and pushed back on the bar so that you have to reselect your skill.  If you hit the enemy well they are in the red bar they will be knocked back and interrupted as well.  So you can really plan knocking back enemies judging by how fast they are on the bar.  Other than that you only can fight with 2 characters and  the enemies can have up to 3.
What makes this a good game to play yourself is the skills that you get.  Now it isn't as in depth as a skill tree is, but it has enough depth so that you can choose what you want each character to do.  Each skill has two forms as well, the solo one which hits one enemy and the all version which hits all enemies.  The all version takes a lot longer to get off though.  Also if you play the game on the casual difficulty, not only can you avoid most fights to beat the game, you get more exp.  In the expert version you can finish the game at level 50 but on casual it's around 70.
Expert difficulty also creates the importance of the crafting system where you actually have to use items and upgrades to survive.  There is a crafting system in the game called Oculli which isn't explained so much, but it isn't that convuluted that you wouldn't understand it with some practice.  The game also gives you a lot to use for crafting.  Basically they upgrade your strength in certain aspects.  Like the red Oculli gives your character fire damage and the blue one water damage.  They also give you defencive boosts, based on which Oculli is put where.
Overall I'd say this game is good, but don't expect the most immersive rpg mechanics or characterization, that other rpg's like final fantasy have.  This game took me about 14 hours to complete, but I did enjoy my experience.  And it was nice to be able to play an rpg that wasn't going to take me 100 plus hours to beat.  I'd recommend this game to people who want to play an rpg that isn't too hard or takes too much time to get into.  I also recommend playing this game on expert difficulty, which is the way it was meant to be played.

+Excellent, deep turn-based combat that provides room for emergent gameplay and different strategies. There are no random encounters and each fight is deliberately crafted by the developers. Despite playing D:OS for over 100 hours, I never once found the combat repetitive or tedious, which is an impressive feat considering the tendency in turn-based games for the player to develop a methodical, unexciting approach to most fights.
+Long campaign that can last 100+ hours and heavily rewards exploration. Most quests are interesting; no generic fetch quests. There is minimal handholding and you will have to talk to NPCs, read everything and search everywhere to have an idea of what to do next.
+Well implemented "morality" system where choices are not clear-cut black and white, and where most decisions have meaningful consequences. For example, you can kill almost anybody in the game and steal almost anything, but you will have to deal with the repercussions of that character's death or getting caught. Most quests are very open-ended and there are multiple ways to resolve each one.
+Playing on Hard, I found the difficulty to be challenging but fair. The enemies generally have access to the same abilities as you, and at no point did I feel that the computer was being cheap. Generally speaking, most of the classes are well balanced, and while some are stronger earlier in the game, other builds become more useful later on. You will have a better experience if you try to role-play and not powergame, i.e. don't try to min-max optimize your characters and builds and in return the fights will be more fun and more rewarding. I would have liked for the bosses to be a bit more difficult, though. I found that only two or three were significantly more difficult than the normal enemy encounters.
-Despite my earlier comment, some game mechanics are poorly balanced or implemented, which can lead to exploitable/ annoying situations. Because the class system is so flexible, there is no real need to specialize (unless roleplaying) and there isn't much replay value as a result.
-The item mechanics in this game aren't that good. The inventory system is clunky, especially if you have a tendency to hoard crafting ingredients and consumables, like I do. Not a fan of the randomized loot. Some chests will be guaranteed to give some high level loot, but the stats on those items will be randomized, meaning you can get a crap rare item or an excellent one from the same chest on 2 different occasions. More unique items would have been better. In addition, aside from a few recipes, the crafting system is a bit gimmicky.
-Story was interesting at first, but it changes in scope too quickly for my tests, and I could not empathize with the characters after a certain point. Some people disliked the light-hearted writing; I personally did not have an issue with it but it is worth pointing out that the writing has more of a humorous tone than a serious one.
Overall I would rate this game 5/5 (not implying it is perfect). This was one of the best games to come out of 2014 and it was a great addition to my library. If you're a fan of "classic" style RPGs, I would highly recommend this game.

A great RPG.
Pros.:
++ Skills/spells are important. Simple teleport (no damage, 1 turn cooldown) may be the deadliest "weapon" in the right place. Well placed immobility/slow spells can turn deadliest one hit overkill enemies into chickens in a slaughterhouse even if you have just a few small knifes. A lot of tactics and lore. Of course you will learn some typical tricks, combos and weaknesses, but still the game will bring you new tactical puzzles/challenges every once in a while.
++ Quests are relevant. Not just the nowadays usuall go there and bring/kill me that one. There is some story behind every single one of them.
+ There are some nice or funny surprises/conversations scattered through the story/maps, Which help the game be more alive.
Cons.:
-- Quest logbook. Worst ever may be a bold statement, still not much lied. You may spend 1/4 (20 hours anyone?) of the game just trying to figure out where you have to go. What for? The game is long enough to sell it proud without such "extension". In the end you may find yourself googling. Which sucks.
It's really ok to hide the question marks from the heads. But once you got the quest, read the lost and found letters, gather the hints... why the hell can't you find all the details (names, places) in logbook after? You still have to reread 40 letters in your inventory, to find the right ones. And then try to remember on which map in which place you actually met everyone or that weirdly named cave was.
- I did miss more NPC/party voice. Both diversity in towns and speach in critical moments . That could have made the game so much more alive. Especially considering the really well done voice quality in those rare cases where it is used.
Short:
Definitely recommend.

Reminiscent of a free-to-play MMO, Black Desert has a strong presentation and flashy appeal, which sadly fades quickly. The game is generally unimpressive and is a shallow MMO that does nothing new, and is about as generic as they come. The best word I can find for this game, is mediocre. Mediocrity permeates from every facet, across the board from graphics to gameplay. It isnt terrible, but it is far from great.
The graphics are deceiving, because when you look at screenshots or pictures of the character class models, they look superb. Character creation screen is also misleading, and once you actually get into the game the models suddenly look crappy. The textures, geometry, and shading is bad and makes the game look dated. The foliage looks especially terrible, which is unfortunate since the world of BD is full of lush green plains and forests, that would otherwise look good. There are a lot of garish color tones and it can be hard to even look at the game. Maybe I just had too high of expectations,  but considering this is a game that was released in 2017 I think its a fair judgement. (GTX 1070/i7 6700K 4.0ghz, max settings @ 1080p)
The audio is very irritating. I find it hard to appreciate how the Korean culture thinks squealingly high voices are considered cute and adorable. You have this little black spectre that serves as a guide and quest giver, and its deafening shrills that emit from its mouth are headache inducing. And you'll be hearing a lot of those, hopefully a mod will release that will axe its audio files or something. The squeals and moans that come from female characters, from generally every type of action/movement is also annoying. They are also all suspiciously sexual sounding. The music is the cliche fantasy land orchestra that you would expect from a game like this, not bad but not noteworthy either.
Gameplay is great, its very fast paced and stylish looking. Its a relief considering most MMO games have auto attacks like WOW. It feels almost like Nier Automata, and is full of combos that all feel powerful and look cool. The quests are intensely grindy and repetitive. Despite that, I find it hard to critique an MMO game based on repetitive and bland quests, since thats almost a requirement for the genre.

I played last year for 6 month when the game was relatively fresh.

First, it's everything you expect from a korean grinder and nothing more, well graphic is pretty awesome though ...
There were some major updates to bring the game on par with the Korean version but in its core it's the same.

I talked to a couple of people from my old guild who played a little longer to verify my thoughts.

The game itself is fun to a part, till you want to reach the endgame content and there the problem starts.

- Grinding:
You have to grind a lot and by a lot i mean at least a couple hours per day. At least you can decide between monsters or materials for crafting.

- Drop rates:
Abysmal, you see people getting tons of rare items but trust me you won't be one of them.
Short story time: Once one of my Guild Members was farming Ogres, which are over farmed like hell and there are only 10(!) on the whole map with a 10min respawn timer. So he got the 0.001% item two times in a night while other members farmed them for month and got nothing. As i said korean grinder ...

- Crafting:
Most of the stuff you craft is utterly useless, the best weapon and armor are drops crafting is only for money making nothing more.I was Alchemy master rank 8, potion are rarely used so if you play the game don't be an Alchemist ;)

- PVE
Grinding, though there were some "instances" put in one of the updates but its endgame and you will need a lot of time to see them. Story sucks, no need to make an extra point

- PVP is good, i mean rly good. I have to say that i'm not the average player, i played at least 8h a day including class training and group pvp training. If you don't have that time or you are not a genius don't buy this game. 1on1 is kinda balanced GvG is also quite good. The problem here is that big guilds will dominate, which results in a big zerg and the Guild with more aoe classes will win. Here I have to point out, the guild i was in, was lead by a member of the WoW guild Method and every single player was on a high skill lvl. Which made pvp (even against superior numbers) a lot of fun.
And ofc open pvp, enjoy getting ganked all day long with no gear as a new player and yes no catch up mechanic you are just ♥♥♥♥ed for the next year.
The end content of the game is PVP if you are not into hardcore PVP dont play this game.

- Gear
Upgrading gear is pretty frustrating, if you never played a korean mmo it's going to be really frustrating.
You upgrade your gear, from lvl 1-20, till 15 you are fine you have a chance to fail which will cost you a couple of million each try but nah don't worry you will somehow get there ... From 15 - 20 you can fail and your weapon will go down in lvl. Example: lvl 16 Weapon upgrade to lvl 17 -> goes down to lvl 15 and you are back the start …
For people who start new, there i no catch up mechanic, you are just ♥♥♥♥ed, 100% ♥♥♥♥ed no ones wants you because of your gear sucks as said in “- PVP”. ´You need at least 6 month or a lot of money to catch up.
Edit: Did i mention your accessories can get destroy if you fail to upgrade them. :D

- And of course P2W:
Yeah game is P2W. Too much benefits from the Item Shop and ofc you got the monthly subscription which without you don't need to play the game. Even the cosmetic items, which cost 20 euro per complete costume gives benefits for you character. Pet bonus, crafting points and and and ... the game in one big cash grab that's why they moved to steam … i spend 800 euros in this 6 months money is gone for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.
Edit: You can sell Shopitems via the Auctionhouse.
Edit:Hacking and boting:
One example was the automated fishing bot, which is basically implemented in the game and one of the selling points (lol). The normal afk fisher got one fish every 2-3mins the bot was able to get one every 10 seconds. Fishes sell for a high price and fishing is one of the easiest way to make money. With the bot you were able to 20 fold you revenue out of fishing. Daum was not able to do something against it till i stopped playing. Guess that's still there policie ...

TL:DR:  Overall i would give the game 40/100, for some time killing its okay but to play it over a longer time its just too repetitive (like all the mmos atm). AND IT IS A PVP GAME GO PLAY DOTA OR CS:GO, IT'S AT LEAST BALANCED

Most RTS games are extremely complex. Often you need to accomplish A and B before C can be completed. Boid takes an entirely new spin on an old favorite by simplifying it into something that is easily digestable, even if you only have a few minutes to sit down and play. The accessibility of Boid is certainly one of its strongest tenants. Basic units come from Spawn Pools, then they are put into a larger pool to turn them into the class of your choosing as identified by the symbols. The classes are quite varied, though most maps don't feature all the classes at once. Scouts are fast but lack defense, Crabs have massive attack but low speed. There are healers, poison-support units, and even kamikaze bombers! Figuring out how you prefer to coordinate them is great fun, and there is really no wrong answer which leads to a world of replayability. Once you have a sizeable force, you can set them up as a barricade to repel enemy intruders. The troops will need to be reinforced after each skirmish, which kept me delightfully rushing about the pool upgrading units and trying to keep my army of microorganisms bolstered enough to repel any danger. Some classes do counter each other, which means you'll probably want a mixed regiment of units to protect each of your spawn pools. If all you have is Crabs and Basics and an enemy Bomb shows up, they'll all be blown to smithereens... One shot with a ranged Gun unit could've saved them if only I had the foresight. This class-based RTS is simple, fast-paced, brutal, and I love it. Let's take an even deeper look at Boid.
One of the first things I feel I should mention is the online multiplayer. Currently there is only a 1v1 mode, but any game that is released with the capability for some raw PvP gives me a warm fuzzy feeling. Bots send tiny regiments of units to scout your defenses, however most player fights end up as a giant war of attrition. While bot battles are usually short and succinct, PvP battles can rage on for upwards of thirty minutes. The center of the battlefield becomes a killing field, wave after wave of units, some too young to even have a class, sent to die for your glory. It reminds me a lot of trench warfare, both players sacrificing everything they have in order to gain just a few more feet of leverage. Then, just when you think you've pushed them into hiding, a regiment of scouts executes a flanking attack that decimates your forward force. The action is extremely tense, which impresses me to no end mostly because of the simplicity of the graphics. Everything is portrayed in minimal detail, but at the same time, nothing feels left out. At no point did I feel confused about if a unit was functioning, from the Bomb's rippling explosion to the Medic's healing wave, everything feels wonderfully pieced together. Currently the map selection is minimal, but Steam Workshop support will soon be added, allowing you to create your very own microscopic battleground.
Unfortunately, the game doesn't have any background music during the actual battle. The music that is offered during the selection menu is quite fitting though, and when ordered to move the different classes will utter unique cries of confirmation. You start to feel connected to your microscopic minions. Proud of their victories, though when they are defeated it is only due to your tactics. Strategies must be shifted based on the layout of the map, and the spawn/class pools. The game never felt over my head, and even features a brief tutorial. I'm extremely impressed at how easy it is to isolate a class, or break off a regiment from your main force. There are red pulses on the edge of your screen which let you know if you're being attacked, and in which direction. If one you capture a pool, or get one of yours taken the entire screen will flash. There are very important minor details that make the game feel much more alive, especially when facing a top level player. A squad of Scouts can be sent to distract at one spawning pools, while the bulk of your fighting forces takes another. I desperately want to see four-player maps with every unit available. Currently the price sits at $3, which is unbelievable for what is offered. The price will increase when workshop support is added, and again when single-player campaigns are finally offered. My suggestion would be to jump on this bandwagon as soon as possible. Boid offers a swarm of fun and can only get better. I'm positive that with Workshop support, this microscopic game could blow up bigger than it ever dreamed.
There is little to say negatively about Boid. It does feel a bit bare bones, but for a recently released Early-Access title it is extremely playable. The player-base is currently quite tiny so you might be waiting for a while to hop into any PvP battles, but hopefully that will be remedied in-part with this review. I feel that the class UI could be cleaned up slightly with the addition of hotkeys, since the cursor really does need to be everywhere at once in this sort of action-RTS. Right now the game can become anything, and while hope springs eternal, reality is usually a lot less kind. I hope to see different modes implemented aside from direct obliteration of your opponent. Perhaps a hard-point or capture-the-flag gamemode? Then there are the aforementioned bigger maps... Boid looks to me like to will be able to deliver. Much care obviously went into its creation. As proven by the variety of options to select from, including something called "Colorblind Mode", basically changing all the green/red in the game to blue/yellow... An interesting concept, but one I didn't end up applying, even as a colorblind person. Still the gameplay is blazing fast fun, and one would be crazy to complain about MORE options. Thanks to tinyBuild and Mokus for a fantastic game that will keep me coming back for a long time to come.

Do you want to experience every fantasy MMO ever with very little to distinguish itself from the competition? Yes? Then Black Desert Online is right up your alley!
Do you want something different with a unique feeling world and unique gameplay? Yes? Then avoid this at all costs...
BDO is alright, but it offers very little "new" to the genre to help distinguish itself from other MMO's.
Good:
Combo system is interesting. Not "good" per se, but "interesting". Kinda odd I put it in the good column huh?
Character creator: This has a ton of different options, you can select individual body parts to lengthen, widen, etc. You can do pretty much everything you want (within reason).
Bad:
Class customization. Want to play a wizard? Great, you'll be just like every other wizard ever! Warrior? Great, you are now Warrior #2003023403820482! Congratulations, you're now the 12 billionth iteration of the same exact character!
World: As I mentioned at the start, this game feels like every fantasy MMO before.
Menuegeddon: Menu menu menu and they all convey no information while overwhelming you with nothing. Not even that, they don't even look good, like they came from the early 90's.
Overall, a pretty "meh" game. I see no reason you couldn't just go play any of the other more streamlined MMO's available. The combo system is the only real innovation, yet I never felt it added enough to justify the time investment. MMO's, good ones, can take years of your time, and I just can't, for the life of me, see how this game is worth that investment.

You land in South Park, an silent and peaceful mountain little town. As new kid, that you customize as you like and land in an epic LARPing session. Joining either Cartman’s Humans or Kyle’s Elves, all dressed in amusingly bad makeshift cosplay outfits. True to the show, things escalate wildly and hilariously, leading to conspiracies involving the government, aliens, and Taco Bell.
You and your single extra party member (that you will unlock in South Park regulars, though only one can fight with you at a time) take turns battling formations of enemies, be it the Gingers, crazy homeless guys, aliens, and more. Typical buffs and debuffs are ably skinned in screwed up fourth grader verbiage mixed with mana powered spells and timed button press attacks and blocks to keep you on your toes during combat. It keeps things simple enough while still leaving room for some tactical depth.
Jew class over the archetypal Fighter, Thief, and Mage options, but the differences between them are small. No matter what you choice you can get melee enhancing gear and carving up foes with a blade just as well as a Fighter. All classes eventually learn special farting magic (a crude parody of Skyrim’s Dragon Shouts).
A convenient fast travel system eases post exploration navigation, but various quests provide plenty of enticing reasons to comb the town throughout the adventure. Classic songs like “Taco-Flavored Kisses” and “Kyle’s Mom is a B****” are deployed with deft comedic subtlety on radios and in shops, and you absolutely must listen carefully for the particularly perfect use of Bigger, Longer, & Uncut’s “Blame Canada.”
Funny achivements, quests, enemies, plenty of collection items like Pokemons? Or equipment from sword of warriors to wands and staffs of jews? Goth armor and warrior armor, even valkiria armor for your own likeing or witch.

It's a very niche game made on a tight budget. Expect a lot of reused content (identical dungeons, palette swap enemies), and that everything happens in a VN way, mostly offscreen. If you like JRPGs, you might find the content a little bit too thin.
With that in mind, I'd recommend the game just on this "something" it has that kept me playing. The characters are likeable and the dialogue humorous. The writing is very self-aware and has a lot of references, but it has charm, the references and 4th wall breaking moments are overt enough not to feel forced or heavy-handed. There's some fanservice, but it's not sleazy, just a scene of Neptune getting a bandage bikini early on and later some awkward hugs.
The music is catchy, battle animations and 3d models are well-animated, there's a lot of different weapons and outfits to grind for, and the battle system is complex enough to be interesting throughout the whole game (there's a battle animation button skip under left bumper, which eases the pain of grinding a lot).
Buy it if you'd like a laid-back story and just a bit of challenge. Don't if you don't like moeshit anime.

It's obviously produced by an amatuar team. The production values are functional, and the art quality is all over the place. I've played through seven different endings now (two versions of three different paths and one that seems to have only one version), and the endings are all different... and I mean *really* different, in terms of tone, and even genre. They range from really happy hopeful to dark as ♥♥♥♥ to... well, let's just say the achievement is literally titled, "What is this I don't even..." The logic of the paths generally makes some sort of sense. I had to hint guide some of it, but that's just because I'm impatient and didn't feel like exploring the story web relentlessly until I finally figured certain things out. XCOM is a grid-based tactical game with some fun unit management.  A grid is a two dimensional field in which everything is partitioned off into tiles which all take up the exact same amount of space and have the same shape.  Each tile is arranged on the grid such that it's position in relation to all other tiles is exactly the same as any other tile's position in relation to the tiles that surround it.  Grids can continue on in any direction for as long as they need to.  You can think of grids as a sort of pattern that can be extended or cut short (made shorter or longer), but the pattern will stay the same.  Grids do not need to have a consistent shape, but the patterning of the tiles does need to remain consistent.  If you are still having trouble grasping the idea of grid I can suggest some additional reading:
Metric Spaces by Thomas Wieting (2013) [
]
The Amazing World of Grids by Harold Svenberg (1957)
Grids and Lowest Level Computational Methods by Paul Moore (1989)
If you are still having trouble grasping the concept of grids I suggest you go back and re-read my introductory paragraph with the knowledge that you now have from your additional readings.  Yeah, I realize that that's a bit of a cop-out but I'm kind of at a loss for how to explain this any more clearly to you.  I really thing that you must be overthinking this, a grid is not something that you normally have to explain to people at all.  Even with children who do not know what a grid is you can show them some examples and they'll get the basic idea.  I mean you certainly don't need to be some sort of grid guru just to understand what I'm going to be saying in this review.  You really just need a basic understanding and some common knowledge.
Sorry, I think I came off a bit condescending there.  Let's try this again.  I know you can get this if you just take it slow and try to think critically.  Grids are made up of tiles, tiles are arranged inside of the grid in a constant pattern.  Really the tiles are just subdivisions of the area that the grid covers, a way of splitting up the space into many different parts that all have the same size and shape.
Now come on, don't be so hard on yourself, I KNOW you can do this!  You've come this far and I can't let you give up. Crawl is what happens when the madness, frustration, and heart pounding action of the last few seconds of classic couch co-op games is stretched into 20 minutes. The complex tug and pull between monsters and hero is always changing, and with randomized equipment and maps ensures that no player is ever truly out of the race. The game encourages players to be cautious and through by filling rooms with treasure and goodies for the hero, but every second you spend inside is one your opponents have to try and take your life. The boss encounters are unique and challenging, perfect capstones to the intensity of the crawl proper.
Crawl is the sort of game that takes fellow gamers and makes them friends (or enemies.) It's haunting atmosphere and illustrious pixel art support the frantic and tense gameplay. 9/10, absolutely wonderful.

A synthesized battle droid voice comes over into your ears.
Seconds later, the CIS battlecruiser bursts into chunks, wisps of fire dying in the vacuum of space as sunlight crests the nearby Republic planet.
You chuckle and a "Victory" readout appears before you.
And that's just a moment in Battlefront 2.
- - -
While Star Wars Battlefront 2 is, y'know, ancient at this point, it is still a beauty in gaming and the serious nostalgia trip for so many of us. I, being a late-comer to gaming and Battlefront 2 being one of the earlier console games I played (along with GUN and I believe Flatout), can quickly say that this game is gorgeous and sold the industry to me.
It's massive, it's immersive, it's quick-to-play, and it's
Who doesn't like Star Wars? Well, plenty of people, but... hey, you can't dislike the adorable Stormtroopers.
You've got all the stuff other shooting games do. Guns, people to shoot guns, and some extra things like vehicles. Then there's the space battles, which make an entirely different challenge and one of the most glorious flying experiences in gaming, and then you've got the tactical 'Conquest' part where you put around a giant fleet of spacecraft for your favorite faction in the Star Wars movies.
Rebels, Empire/Republic, CIS: You can play as any of them, which is great fun. Each have their own soldiers and classes, allowing different experiences for every team. It's especially cool to roll around as a droideka, then unfurl and be destroyed by a Jedi. At least you're the envy of your friends.
The battles themselves are manic and titanic. Hoth a devoid planet? Not when you're in the middle of a 100+ person skirmish between Rebels and Imperials. AT-AT action is amazing, until you're taken down by some jerk in a cheap snowspeeder. Maybe it was SKYWALKER?
No.
There's also that option to play as a Jedi or Sith or melodramatic bounty hunter popping up every now-and-then, but they're lame and die too quickly. I don't suggest them. Well, MBH is alright, but who wants to get eaten by a sandpit monster?
There's the few issues, like absurdly dumb AI and logical errors (downwards gravity in space?), but they're far and few compared to the joy this game brings.
I couldn't recommend this enough. And it's only 10 bucks USD!

This is an odd game in that it has several competing elements. The best thing this game has going for itself is that is gorgeous. For every other feature in this game I'm not sure if I like it or not.
Travel: There is no fast travel in this game. However, you can put a way point on your and your character will walk their automatically. This gives you time to enjoy the scenery and look at the many different statistical options.
Crafting: The crafting, gathering, and development system is super extensive. Getting different food ingredients, alchemist items, mining, fishing, etc. There are even layers to build trade routes and hiring NPC workers to gather, trade, and even craft items for you.
Combat: Fun Action RPG style with different combos. At least at the start of the game the combat is super easy. I killed the first 2 bosses without going bellow 90% of my health and I'm carrying around 100 healing potions that I never use.
AFK Rewards: This game actually rewards you for being AFK. You can literally set up and let the game run and you'll get experience and items.
Conclusion 5/10: This game is one part button masher, one part economical management system, one part sandbox open world and one part screen saver. All of these things are good but the overall system is clunky and their is no motivation to play besides get random stuff.
P.S. If you are interested in the game purchase the cheapest version of the game. The other two item packs aren't that useful or fun. You can get most of the items after playing a little in game.

Nitroplus Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel uses flash and style along with countless assist characters to make what would otherwise be a limited fighting game feel fun and exciting, as well as easy to pick up and play.
Nitroplus Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel is both a mouthful of a title as well as a surprisingly fully featured fighting game. Featuring a traditional super gauge and assist system, it seeks to set itself apart from the other fighters by using its diverse cast of characters to change up gameplay greatly. Whether it achieves that is a different story entirely.
The story takes a backseat to the gameplay, as tends to be with most fighting games. It’s pretty unobtrusive and can be skipped extremely easy for those who want to get back into the action, however fans of the series can find comfort in every character having their own unique set of dialogue between fights in the game’s story mode. Unfortunately we couldn’t see for ourselves if there was any kind of full cutscene work for the story, as such a thing would likely be locked behind the final boss of the story mode, which proceeded to beat the snot out of us regardless of how many varied attempts we threw at it. Be prepared for a fight if one wants to beat the entire story mode.
Flashy effects and the Blast system, as well as an incredibly diverse set of absurd supers and assists go a long way towards making Nitroplus Blasterz feel very fun to play. Every impact feels like it has weight, and the amount of options at one’s disposal to move around the opponent also adds a frantic pace to the game, our matches rarely saw the counter drop below seventy seconds. It’s hard to gauge the depth of a fighting game with a limited amount of time and online play being an impossibility before launch, but regardless of how far the complexity goes, it’s definitely a fun and flashy fighter that feels great to play. The game modes offered are the basic necessities - a story mode, an alternative story mode that we failed to unlock, a versus mode for fighting against friends or CPU opponents, and lastly a score attack and online play support to round out the options.
Specifically of note, the Blast system is an interesting addition, as it can be triggered once per fight and causes the super bar to both generate quickly over time, as well as increase the amount of super gained through attacks. Activation also causes a burst animation around the user which takes priority over everything and knocks the opponent back if caught in it, no damage is dealt but it's an easy way to combo break if they're caught in a bad situation and the extra super given as a result helps make a comeback.
As far as the rest of the gameplay goes, it's similar to other fighting games with high, mid and low attacks for mixups, special moves with their own inputs as well as powered up versions that burn super to use, a grab and grab counter system as well as supporting air grabs, and a dash system similar to Skullgirls, where several characters can get some absurd aerial movement going with attacks and jumps/dashes. Movement feels appropriately fast and combat feels very weighty with most of the cast.
Also worth mentioning is pure content, as many modern fighters will charge for things like alternate costumes, and while the number of legitimately different costumes is pretty limited - usually just a swimsuit for select characters - the number of palette changes available on every character from the start can and often does break twenty, which adds a bit of variety and personalization, however slight it may be.
Flashy effects are a staple of fighting games, and Nitroplus Blasterz doesn’t disappoint in this regard, from most supers having short animated cutscenes if they land to the absurd screen effects on even the most basic of special attacks add a lot of flair and personality to the game. That of course just refers to the base characters, each assist has their own unique effect on the battlefield, one of our favorites was a girl who covered the field in ice pillars that knock up the enemy, setting them up for aerial combos or a quick air grab. There’s an absurd amount of variety in the visual effects department, and sound is no slouch either. Everything comes together to present the game as an incredibly fast paced fighter that ought to be fun for a bit with friends in showing off flashy effects.
Content wise, it appeared to be a bit lacking at first glance with a grand total of 14 fighters, something that’s even beaten by Street Fighter V without having to unlock any others, but this was quickly forgiven when after selecting the fighter, an assist menu was presented, allowing two choices out of a whopping twenty. While the fleshed out fighters may be lacking in count, the amount of legitimately varied assists that can be comboed in all sorts of ways by the skilled and creative mean even mirror matches can bring out extremely different play styles from both sides. The number of stages is a non issue as well, they provide some set dressing but no stage hazards of effects to worry about, and the original releases on the PS4 and Vita had post-launch DLC in the form of crossover characters from Senran Kagura and Arcana Heart. Both characters are included free of charge in this PC release.
Similar to other smaller fighting games in comparison to titans like Street Fighter or Dead or Alive, Nitroplus Blasterz exists in a unique space as a relatively inexpensive fighter that’s easy to pick up and play with others. It’s not something to dedicate months learning for EVO, but it’s definitely worth playing if not for the frantic pace and fun supers, then for the variety of fighters and enjoyable combat that feels weighty and flashy in all the right places. While content wise it could be a little better, it’s hard to argue when it’s just so fun to play, not to mention most of the fighting game fans on Steam will be receiving discounts for owning Skullgirls. Definitely worth a look for anyone who enjoys a bit of casual fighting with friends or just wants to experience the variety for themselves.

This game is hands down the best turn based isometric RPG to come out since the late 90s- early 2000s. Its mindblowing. It is everything a true RPG fan could want, depth, story, tactics, customization. So many modern RPGs are dumbed down, basically a siries of "go here, do this" fetch, kill the whatzit, ect quests with little minimap icons to point you along the way.
Not Divinity: Original Sin.  Its challenging. It makes you think, use tactics and your environment in combat, and also to get hidden bits of story. If you just wade in to battle, expect to get pulverized.
Its for the die hard RPG fan. Casual players or people who expect to always win and not talk to people and go places just for more plot are not going to like this. People who want a modern take on the great RPGs of the late 90s are going to think their dreams came true with this one.
I know I did.
As far as the co-op goes, its a cool feature and I suppose some people like it, but I could have totally done without it. Really. RPGs are single player in my world. Fortunately, you can choose a "personality" for the char youre not playing, or just pick the dialogue yourself. If your chars disagree a "rock paper scissors" type game insues, where you get bonuses based on the type of answer you made (if you have a high skill in a type of answer, you get more points) and the winner of that is the one who makes the final choice. Its interesting to say the least.

This is a great effort by Larian worth any RPG fan's time.  I loved Baldur's Gate when it came out and haven't found anything that has captured its essence since quite like D:OS does.  Every system in place here is solid and ripe for improvement in future games.  Battle, crafting, skills, equipment, exploration, dialogue... all of these are fun and seem well thought out (though rock,paper,scissors for charisma/intimidate is just ok).  While there is quite a bit of freedom, players are still somewhat limited in where they can go based on level alone.  I accidentally went to the wrong area at one point, unaware why my %'s to hit were failing (it's level-based), and ended up at a large boss battle I couldn't win.  Luckily, the save & transportation systems made it easy to just go somewhere else.  I will say that the game got a bit repetitive for me once I found a combination of abilities that made all battles easy, but that didn't happen until 40 hours in, so I got my money's worth for sure.  I'm very much looking forward to what's coming next using this same game style.

XCOM integrates a lot of interesting features and systems into its gameplay. I was looking forward to playing it for its tactical turn-based combat system, but found myself having more fun with the base management, research and engineering system. However, it does not come without any faults, I encountered numerous bugs, ranging from the non-saving options menu (that I have to re-configure each time I play) to buggy in-game user interface.
The meat of the game, tactical turn-based combat, was an OK experience (Line of sight system isn't perfect, sometimes an alien is right in front of you and your soldier can't see them, I didn't enjoy the Overwatch mechanic, and randomly activating 3 alien camps with one movement is not fun). The best part of this game is the squad system, you get to customize and outfit all your soldiers;  there being different classes, abilities trees, weapons and equipment.
Sidenote: I do criticize Firaxis for releasing XCOM: Enemy Within as a standalone game on consoles, but on PC you have to buy the $32 base game XCOM: Enemy Unknown before you can play the $32 Enemy Within, which is just the same campaign as XCOM:EU with some extra missions and updates. I would recommend XCOM: EU, but buy Enemy Within only if you like the base game and if it goes on sale.

Xcom... well, to put it bluntly GET THIS GAME! The original Xcom was about 18 years ago, and it was miraculously good. And now, finally, a new one is here. It sticks to the same premise as the old one, some of the same aliens, same idea, same combat ect... The difference is, this game is SO much newer, and by that i mean the game is 100x more advanced than that of the old one. The base hub is now an ant farm looking window, where you can research new alien tech in the lab or build new weaponry in the engineering department and foundry. You can now customize your soldiers down to great detail, changing names, nicknames, race, voice, face, hair and more. You can't add as much equipment as you could in the old Xcom such as backpacks and pockets, but you can still choose their weaponry and equipment. In the old Xcom you could pick up alien weapons from the ground, but in this one you can't (at least not straight away) as when you kill an alien, it's weapon explodes into weapon fragments which you can use in your research. In later stages of the game (or earlier, depending on how well you're doing) when you have researched plasma weaponry, you can actually pick up plasma guns and use them in the barracks. There are 4 classes in the game, sniper, heavy, assault and support. Sniper is very self explanitory (as are most of the classes) focused on dealing heavy damage from far away, they are quite slow and require strategic placing as they can't move and fire on the same turn with out being promoted a number of times. Heavy is equipped with a rocket launcher, dealing massive damage, they can take hits and deal them with their LMG's. Support classes have smoke grenades with lowers the % chance of hitting anyone inside them. They can also be leveled up to specialised with smoke or manually equipped med-kits. Assault class is equipped with a shotgun, they deal alot of damage but have a hard time hitting enemies. They can dash and fire on the same turn, making them useful at saving teammates from combat. One of the research projects in the foundry is S.H.I.V which is a robot that takes the place of a soldier, it has an attached minigun and deals high damage, they can also suppress enemies, disabling movement and greatly reduces the chance of them hitting you. The turn-based combat is focused on the cover system, leaving your troops out of cover is moronic as the chances of an enemy hitting you is almost certain. Cover can be destroyed, forcing you to thing about where you move each turn. when you select a troop there is a highlighted blue area and a highlighted yellow area, if you move in the blue area you can shoot (unless the moved troop is a sniper) or go into overwatch mode (if an enemy moves, your troop will take a reaction shot in the enemies turn). If you move in the yellow zone which is way longer than the blue zone you cannot do another action unless you are assault class and use the ability. The aim of the basic game mode (which is presented as an urgent meeting in the mission control room) is go to an area of your choosing out of a choice of three (each with it's own rewards) and take out all the aliens there. The other game modes include; rescue a VIP, rescue civilians from an alien area, Take out and recover an alien ship, invade an alien base and more. Each of these brings it's own rewards such as engineers, scientists, money and decreased panic level in that country (the whole idea of Xcom is each country is in the xcom project and relies on you to protect them, the more you dont protect them, the more the panic levels go up and when they are all the way up you lose the country from the project, losing all countries from the project ends the game.) In, and at the end, of every game mode you will recieve research parts such as corpses of aliens, weapon parts, alien flight computers etc. These all need to be researched to progress the game, with key research triggering cut-scenes which actually progress the game,one of these being capture a live alien with the arc-thrower which is essentilly an alien taser. The pro's and con's of this game are:
Pro's:
-An amazing ant farm view system, organizing and recognizing where and what everything is.
-Amazing barracks system with customization that really gets you emotionally attached to your soldiers
-Nail biting, teeth gritting turn based combat
-Almost limitless development as far as research & engineering goes
-Alot of game modes that the original Xcom had, and more
-A brand new multiplayer mode
-Great graphics
-Mod support
-A tutorial that explains combat and the most part of the hub navigation
-Great, cheap DLC
-Great classes and abilities for each soldiers
Con's:
-Multiplayer is only VS with selected units, no co-op campaign
-No base defence mode like in the original Xcom
-incredibly hard to keep countries in the Xcom project, takes practice and knowledge
-cannot stop soldiers in motion, often resulting in your favorite man running head first into a swarm
Overall this game for me is a 10/10 and a MUST-BUY! i strongly recommend this game for anyone, enjoy! :)

Grim Dawn is an unique gem that managed to do something to me that no other ARPG ever did since Diablo II, which is to suck alway hours of incredible gameplay and keeping your attention with a very intriguing lore. Grim Dawn doesn't really reinvents the wheel, but it surely polishes it further, by bringing a lot familiar gameplay aspects from older ARPG games, especially from Titan Quest, it's "ancestor", like the Dual Class system, that allows the player to mix two different masteries, creating lots of possibilities for builds, along with the amazing Devotion system, where the player receives a Devotion point by restoring shrines scattered around the world of Cairn and then can spend these points to unlock various constellations on the Devotion window; each constellation granting lot's of passive bonuses, while some granting extra skills that you can attach to your mastery skills, bringing build diversity to a whole new level. Oh, and let's not forget bout the hidden walls/chests scattered everywhere... I have over 5000 hours recorded on Steam, and I'm still finding a new chest or breakable wall somewhere...
Grim Dawn is definitely one of the best games ever made, and I'm very glad and proud to be able to enjoy it ever since the Early Access period, and my only regret is to not have backed it earlier!

I finished one, and started the other hoping it would be better, but it wasn't. I can't remember the last time a game had me hitting the screenshot button as often as this one.
We're two episodes in and I'm only into the first act of episode two, but this is a beautifully rendered game with intriguing characters and a gripping storyline. Yes, it helps if you're a fan of the books or the show and you know going in that whatever happens will not affect the overall storyline and that it's the focused story of one family in the north of Westeros with the occasional cameo of better known characters from George R. R. Martin's saga, but what it does is give you people to care about, scenes that are "around the edges" of the main story and a story that takes place in it's own sub universe of the larger tale.
This isn't for people who want to know what would happen if they gathered an army and marched on King's Landing, rather, it's a story for fans who want to explore the effect events in the main story have on the "background" houses.
Keep that in mind when I say I highly recommend this game. Controls are simple enough and it's even something you can play with other people in the room, almost deciding by committee how the story should proceed. In that sense, as someone who grew up reading "Choose Your Own Adventure" books as a kid, I'm enjoying the hell out of this.
Hopefully they can keep the production schedule up more than Martin can.

This is one of the best and newest ideas for a game that i have seen in a long time. Very unique. Inside by Playdead is its closest relative. Exept for better in almost every way. Roll over, Playdead  ; )
Graphics are 8.5/10, atmosphere is INCREDIBLE 9.99/10. Music is good enough for a good game 7.5/10. The camera angles are interesting, but are fluid and if anything add to the experience. The story is really good 9/10, and this game has NO dialouge. NONE. Wow.
All the characters, helpful ones and dreadful ones, are unique, fluid, creepy, and a solid 9/10. The scariness factor i think comes from how you escape and avoid the antagonists. Quite a bit of suspense, but nowhere near too much at all. There are a couple jumpscares, but the scary part isnt always the shock value the moment it happens... 7.5/10 for overall scares. One of the enemies is downright terifying and might bump up that score a tad for the easily frightened.
And for anyone wondering, the camera angles might suggest otherwise, but this game has Complete 3D movements for everything, unlike Playdead's games and other similar puzzle-platformers.
Oh, and even though the game is a little pricey, the Complete Edition adds a good 3+ hours of gameplay that intertwines a new but previously seen character and storyline, but doesnt add to the base game's storyline. Which i think is a good thing. The Base Game is roughly 5-6 hours, and more if you go achievement hunting... Or find a chair ( yes, a chair ) that may be the funniest purposeful glitch in a game, ever. Look up some youtube videos if you want to find it...
Final Verdict...  9/10 _ This is a must have game. Better than Limbo and Inside. And that's saying something

Half-Life 2 is my favourite game of all time, without exception. I honestly believe that every single person who is capable of doing so should at least try playing it. Its predecessor, its sequals and its mods are extraordinary too. But none of them have captured my heart quite as much as the first one I played.

Ultimately a good game, though it has it's flaws.
It's main draw-in and positive aspect is it's art style and charactization. Jokes are funny (though they will get old), characters look gorgeous, and this game is waifu city.
It's biggest flaw is it's game balance.
As a gamer, I tend to look a lot into studying mechanics and seeing methods into how to play the game without resorting to grinding (game's a lot duller that way). What I found was the best way to beat the game is to use buffs, debuffs, and use Exe abilities (your limit breaks essentially) above everything else. However, this ends up being a really simple and honestly disappointing result.
In the end, characters are either too specialized towards combat (meaning you can't use who you want), or the bosses themselves are built to be a DPS check either though insane health regen or having a high guard meter, on top of having an insane HP pool. This makes debuffs + EXE spamming the most efficient way to beat battles.
However, this gripe can be minor in the grand scheme of things. This doesn't quite do that, but it's a fun game that you can play to your liking. I may come back and do challenge runs with this, but to anyone who's looking for an indepth battle system you should look elsewhere. If you just want good fun and look at gorgeous art work and engage in waifu battles with your friends, this is definitely a good game for that.

Remember a silly game called "Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars"?
That became Rocket League.
Now, this game has a likewise silly title and a ridiculous concept, but I pray that one day the dev will make "Robot League" and it'll become an international success because this game is crazy fun.
You're a robot on a wheel; you slide across the arena and try to pick up balls to toss against other robots to make them explode. This simple concept is applied to a plethora of game modes (FFA/Team/Elimination/CTF/Hoops/Race/...) and, coupled with the flashy graphics and amazing soundtrack, manages to keep the experience fresh for that "just 5 more minutes" effect at 2am.
You might not see a huge amount of players on the charts but don't be fooled: I was having fun with as little as 10 players "playing now", plus the bots are surprisingly competent.
9.5/10 - A purely skill-based arena "shooter" with quick & furious matches and a non-toxic community.

You can beat it in half to a third of that time if you just complete the missions and avoid leveling up (in other words, if you have no idea what this kind of game is about, but just want to admire the beautiful artwork).
I recommend this game for people who ordinarily prefer side-scrolling adventure games, but also appreciate great art, truly inspiring art production, and who may want to try a little RPG style fighting.  There are TONS of hidden treasures throughout this game, and in my opinion that is one of the best things about it.  You can't just click in one way.  10 hours into it, more advanced gamers will probably want to accelerate and skip battles (you can speed up the game a lot by skipping fights, and by clicking the option to make the fight speed faster); but light-gamers and those new to RPG, or those just loving the art, will want to savor the game.
Like others, I do feel the end of the game wasn't anti-climatic, but could be improved.  But hey, this game isn't 50 bucks or anything, it is WELL WORTH THE MONEY at 20 bucks or less, and you will get play time out of it.  You can keep playing after you beat the game though, once the credits are over.  So that's kinda nice.  Once beaten, you really wouldn't play it often afterwards, though.  But thats what other games are for.  The controls are pretty good for movement, very fluid, VERY good graphics relating to that movement too, but the menu system is a bit clunky.
Overall, highly recommended under 10 bucks; an art piece worth 20 bucks; and a no-brainer under 7 bucks.
Hope there is a sequel with an ending as beautiful as the game itself.

First Impressions:
Boid is an RTS similar to that of Eufloria, Oil Rush, and Planets Under Attack. Unlike Eufloria, certain bases are dedicated to spawning units while others are not. Instead, other bases allow you to convert units from "basic" to something else with each unit class having its own strengths, weaknesses, and stats. It's a very tactical game and the AI is incredibly challenging, even on the "easy" difficulty setting. A map editor will be introduced down the line which I'll be interested to try out. I would have liked the ability to be able to set the number of AI opponents...at present, it seems like maps only support a total of two players. It would be fun to see what a three or four player game would look like, I think. $3 is a good value for what the game currently offers.
