I'm going to be very kind with this title since it is free and I know some of it's messy development story. You can forgive the art style which goes from good to more like someone tossed in the concept art pieces and called it a day. Characters are interesting enough and it doesn't have a heavy handed Soviet storyline which I part suspected. Actually rather ignores a lot of that and just uses the Soviet era as a setting. Characters come off a bit better because of it.
However, I can't be totally kind with the writing. The first major offense is the emotional attachment between the characters. Aside from Slavya who is pretty much the poster girl for the game, and Lena who clearly is pegged as the second choice girl to Slavya, the MC (main character) is pretty much at odds with the others. The problem is the writing team focused too hard on making the story neutral and I suspect they didn't really develop the other character's as heroines till later. Probably only had 2 pegged for the initial project.
Up until day 6, the story you can consider is in neutral arc. It's literally harem mode as all these girls throw themselves at the MC but no one really gets picked. What this causes is moments where there is clearly some good moments between the MC and one of the heroine, then he's back to being slug boy and wanting nothing to do with anyone.
His character is probably the biggest hinderance to the story as he's just not believable at times. Specially his reactions. Again this is mostly due to the length of the neutral segment of the story. By the time the individual stories start coming forward, he comes off as just merely going with the flow and not really caring.
There are other weaknesses in some of the characters. One seems to have multiple personalities which doesn't come out till the end and makes you wonder why the MC is willing to overlook the fact she is borderline homicidal. She even gets probably the best ending of them all as the others have rather cookie cutter endings.
Really a lot of this could have been written better but I think what you'll see here is complications from design decisions which just snowball later. It won't be Katawa Shoujo. Not by a long shot. Even the weakest story arcs of Katawa will shine brighter than this. But it's not a bad use of time. I'm certainly glad to have played this.
All in all, it really is a mixed bag. From a story perspective I'd maybe give it a 7/10 tops. Adding in the art issues and general quirks from it's development, probably a 6/10 at best. I hope for the future sequel as I hope they learned a lot from this game's development. But we'll see.

Silly as frick. The story isn't as consistently, jaw-droppingly inspired in its absurd escalations as SR3, but the game plays way better. As a counterpoint to GTA 5, which was the deathknell of the open-world crime game by way of being mired in its conventions and weirdly vicious approach to everything, SR4 is the deathknell by way of showing the absolute limits of what you can do with the formula. What I mean is, within the first hour you get superpowers that let you jump really high, run really fast, and basically fly. Combined, all three of these make stealing in a car, driving around and committing crimes seem antiquated and ridiculous. It's faster and more satisfying to super-run through cars, super jump across rooftops, and fly.
It is hard to talk about what happens in the game without giving away huge spoilers, but let's just say that its entire tone is a very knowing sense of the word "badical." It takes itself very seriously, even when the things it is taking seriously are how totally badass it was that you just climbed a really tall tower and got to the top, or how a confrontation with the alien overlord starts with you, the President of the United States, jumping out of the huge 8-barrel POTUS-branded AA cannon that is stationed on the White House lawn, and running at the crashed alien scout you just shot down, jumping at the front window and shooting it out with a pistol and immediately engaging in a Rowdy Roddy Piper/Keith David "They Live"-esque brawl with said overlord.
Anyone who takes it seriously and makes a character that looks remotely realistic is absolutely playing the game completely wrong and seems to have missed the pitch slider on the voices. The game is basically Your Fricking Ridiculous Power Fantasy: The Game, and is designed around both exceeding your wildest expectations while also subverting them. If there is one thing that the game is willing to critique, it is itself; its existence, your desire to play it, and the video game industry as a whole. It's never condescending when it does this, and comes across as the wet fever dream of a designer at the end of their life, transcribed via dying breaths, and developed as a celebratory eulogy to everything that once was. Its comments are made with a light touch, even when the game itself is so intent on destroying the world and starting over.
Great game.

Grim Dawn may be a little harder to get into than most hack n' slashes, but it's crafted with an old-school gaming approach coupled with newer solutions found in the latest games.
Rich, dark atmosphere has a surprising amount of depth and choices that impact gameplay. While the storyline isn't that involving (saving the world from invading monster factions and learning why), seeing how the people in-game are affected definitely is. Under all this there's plenty of cleverly hidden lore and hard-to-find secret areas.
Pros:
+Good twist on typical skill tress, where you select two classes and find synergy between them, and decide how deeply you invest into a class
+Devotion is a system of common abilities that can back up the weakness of your character. For example, if you lack survivability, you can go for a number of defensive procs. The shrines for these devotion points are found throughout the world, which encourages exploration
+Very cool bosses, tough dungeons, good enemy variety
+An interesting faction system to make the grind matter a little more
+Powerful legendary items that are rarer than in most ARPGs, making them more prestigious
+After 200 hours, there's still so much to do
Cons
- Netplay experience may vary
- Often doesn't feel rewarding enough. You'll have a very hard time finding legendaries for your build, may have to trade
- Feels grindy. It takes a lot of time to slog through all the difficulties to get to Ultimate, and farming infamy for the enemy factions can be very tedious
With hundreds of build combinations, an expansive world, and the ability to play with friends, Grim Dawn breathes new life into the old-school hack n' slash games. It may feel too grindy at times, but the combat is crisp and satisfying at all times.

TL;DR Decent Titan Quest mod that can be recommended ONLY to die-hard fans of TQ and Diablo. However, if you are new to the genre or looking for a complete story, you should look elsewhere.
* Quite addictive loot oriented ARPG. Twin brother of Titan Quest, sister of Torchlight, cousin of Diablo, 1st cousing once removed of Incredible Adv. of Van Helsing, teenage grandkid of Path of Exile
* Good, not great, but good music
* Stable. Had only 1 crash over the span of 60+ hours.
* Potions and currency picked up automatically
* A lot of inventory room, which reduces runs to the shop. Although Torchlight-like pet would be better.
* Some of the lore is very dark, grim and written well.
* Couple references to movies and books
* Unfinished story that probably will be complete with the upcoming DLC
* Gets repetitive, but it is inevitable with most ARPG. Only two types of quests: kill or find something by killing
* A single cutscene and no noticeable transitions or stories between Acts
* Confusing UI elements and some gameplay mechanics
* Mostly boring loot, that does not add much beside higher stats before the end-game.
* No quest pointers on the map unless you are close to the destination
* Can not add map markers to return to places you were not able to fully explore
* Gets quite easy (on Veteran) after a few hours and you have to finish the game several times to unlock next difficulties
* For the most part, uninspiring locations feel the same and have similar layout
* Unable to fully respec, meaning that you can sink 50 points (~17 levels, which is 1/3 by the end of 1st playthrough) into a class that you might not even use.
I feel rather robbed after finishing Grim Dawn. I was expecting something surprising or exciting to happen. Maybe there is an unusual boss coming up? Or a complicated puzzle? New game mechanics or minigame? What about a mind exploding twist in the main story?
Grim Dawn is disappointing, unless you are a loot junkie and really need to have all the legendaries the game can offer. Who knows, maybe it will be a finished game in a few years once all DLCs are released.

It's a tactical sci-fi strategy/management game in which the Earth is being attacked by aliens. A council is made from different countries all over the world to repel this infestation. as commander of the secret operating base and commander of your troops , it is up to you to allocate your resources to research, facilities, upgrades and items. What this game does really well is rewarding you for things you do well. practically everything you research unlocks a new item, facility or ability. launching satellites will generate more income. I had to restart because my panic levels were too high and three countries had already left the council. In my second run, things are going way smoother and this means I get more rewards. The descriptions of different species of aliens and researches are very interesting to read. The only thing I can judge this game on, is the camera and soldier selection. Sometimes the surrounding area blocks my camera view, and this is not easily solvable by rotating, because other walls would block other parts of the map. This is in no way a game breaker, but more of a nuisance. Don't let it stop you from buying this game, because it's definitely worth it.

Nitroplus Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel is a welcome surprise for anyone who loves Japanese games and fighting games in general. Developed by EXAMU, the creator of the series Arcana Heart, and distributed by XSEED Games and Marvelous USA, this game can excel in the genre even having characters not well known in the West and being a bit more niche than the subgenre air dasher, which by itself is already part of a select niche.
With the inclusion of all the DLCs of the console version, new colors for the characters, scenarios with animated backgrounds, new poses of victory and rebalanced gameplay, the PC version of Nitroplus Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel certainly is the definitive edition.
The game manages to surprise right away, with its very well designed sprites, great amount of animation frames, exciting soundtrack and a narrator that reminiscent of the narrator of Pocket Fighter, which gives a cheerful mood to the game. The execution of the basic moves is easy and if at first glance there seems to be a small variety of movements, the impression soon dissolves, as this is a game that rewards players who are willing to discover secret moves that aren't on the commands list.
Even though it's considered an air dasher, the range of air strikes is moderate if we compare it with Skullgirls and the series Arcana Heart and Marvel vs. Capcom. But when it comes to fun, this game entertains as much as the previous games cited.
* Fun game, chaotic (in a good way) and with a cheerful mood
* Fighting system that encourages players to be creative
* Online mode that allows filtering connection types (ping) to avoid lag
* Each fighter is quite different and there are no clone characters
* Remaping options for keyboard and controller
* Definitive edition of the game, with more content for less price
* A small variety of scenarios (only 10)
* Lack of tutorial and / or challenge mode of combos, to help learning the mechanics and combos
* Impossibility to choose the music played. So if you only play with a character in versus mode, the song will always be the same.

Here's a brief review from a brief amount of time played:
If you like Japanese fighting games like Guilty Gear, BlazBlue, Melty Blood, etc, you'll like this one. I personally prefer Melty Blood over this game.
As for the character roster, I imagine that Saber from Fate/Stay Night will be the biggest attraction to most people. Other than that the roster varies fairly wildly. Many of these characters (Saber included) are from Visual Novels that have not been officially translated and released in English. Even then, some of these games have yet to see any type of English localization. Saya is an exception, as Saya no Uta has recieved an offiicial english release (although it isn't for sale on steam due to adult content). I imagine that Arcana Heart fans might be drawn in by Aino Heart.
Basically what I'm saying is that the average American anime/video game fan will recognize at most a couple of these characters.
As for the story, there isn't much of one. What did you expect? Update - June 11th 2016:
Unfortunatelly I cannot reccomend this game; While definatelly pleasant it gives the feel of being extremely far from being finished; While indeed many features were added to add to the industrialized feel and gameplay, once you [quite quickly] make sure your contracts are working it starts giving no true joy as there is no viable reason to optimiise; additionally - there's a machine that is akin to magic wand; easy to use and extremely powerful, with very low cost in comparison to usability; with some schemes being nearly [if not completely] impossible or unviable to produce without that tool game becomes reduced to 'how to use that specific machine'.
While I had high hopes this game would still be worked upon, I'm afraid it is not the case; Developer's activity on forums ceased shortly after question about roadmap; Maybe, just maybe it will be developed further; but honestly - I can't really say it's probable.
Previous reviews:
This game looks like it has a ton of potential, and is quickly improving; While I cannot reccomend this game just yet, both of updates since creation of this review adressed major problems. For time being pricing might be a little too high for what you can get [most of price is basically paid for promise of future content], yet this game's genre is quite niche. If you like games like this - feel free to get it, though don't get your hopes too high just yet.
In hindsight though - given the rate of change in this game - this deffinatelly has a ton of chances to get reccomendable very soon.
Below you can see the review I made before any updates for this game at the day of release.
==PREVIOUS VERSION OF REVIEW [first release]==
ok, while this game has a ton of potential - it's not yet ready for any release anytime soon; let's be honesst - construction system is raw; production lines leave a ton to be desired, most items initially produced are barely visible on production line;
You can only identify wether or not stuff is working by extreme zoom, and ONLY if you have 'transport lines' that are not part of any module especially annoying with stuff like dropzone->exitzone pairing used with some basic contracts;
Also - production steps are very limited when it comes to production itself; I am wondering wether more machines are sheduled as for now - I am starting to worry about this games' future.
Added information:
I honestly DID try to make one turning slope but - line creation controls are extremely ineffective; they tend to overwirite whatever you have already set up; some machines do not care where input is, despite having quite easily identifiable 'production area' [part with 'lines'] - other machines do not always seem to have well identified operational method [saw comes to mind - 3 'line points' - which is input, which is output, which is both?]
stuff that is supposed to move stuff around also cuts it if moved to far; no reverse setting for machine that seems to have 2 pistons [one up and one ddown].
Additional problem - in windows 10 it tends to crash whenever you accept new contract; For more fun - only contracts tend to be saved via the crash automatically.
Item track laying is at level that makes it barely usable. Case in point - Transport Tycoon [original one] despite having annoying [at times] track laying did not have as big problems when making very short range [1 block] curves that this one has; Making 3 or 4 curves in 4 blocks near another is almost impossible without using tools other than simple 'make route part' mainly because of lack of option of making half-routes. Did I mention this game's tracks ten to be bi-directional? in essence - items can go either way via them? I learned it in surprising way by not necesarily intentional messup of pushing item through wall of rotation system, that later fed that item [after rotating it] back through what was intended as input to this machine, straight to messed up transport line that originally pushed it through machine in question, repeating this cycle ad infinitum. Of course when I later pushed item directly though machine's wall [!] it worked - just as I listed - going ad infinitum.
Only when I pushed item through correct input [cursing midway due to deleting this machine twice due to how transport routes work] it worked as intended. I must admit I did ragequit at that point and decided to write this review without checking how exactly saw works, then again - I did not have trust in this games' engine for it to work as intended in the first place.
In short:
This is EXTREMELY early access; There's very little number of Early Access titles in so raw state. Problematic may be also the store page which focuses this pre-purchase towards music and sounds, that in my opionion - are least important problem of this game for now.
If you have trust in this developer - be my guest - try it; I am afraid I'll have to move to refound page, and check this game in few months, maybe it will be made much more user and player friendly and hopefully - polished at least a little.
For the record - I am big fan of production line/assembly line games, and I can't say I'm enjoying having to write this review, but I hope I'll save some factory fans some time with it.
UPDATE 1 : within a day of this review first update came fixing quite a few of these issues; while I did not see some changes that could help, it's a very good sign; let's see what happens next.
TL;DR - Not yet, wait a bit; it's changing for good.

I picked up Everlasting Summer in early January 2016, because I was bored and curious what kind of game this is. I had never played a visual novel before, so I didn't really know what to expect, but this game completely got to me.
You play as this man in his late 30s who has a boring life, he is anti-social and spends most of his time alone on his computer in his flat. He goes to a class reunion and falls asleep in the bus. When he wakes up he notices he in a 1980s Russian pioneer camp. He also turns out to be 17 years old again. He is far away from home, in a different reality even. He stays there for a week and then goes home with the same bus
In this camp he meets all kind of different characters, most of them are girls and he can get attached to them. This leads up to 13 different endings, which take quite some time to complete, but are very story rich and interresting. I would say it is kinda a mind♥♥♥♥ story, if you have done several endings at some points you simply don't know what reality is anymore.
The music is very beautiful and probably the best part of the game, combined with the story. The artwork is good as well, but not amazing-like.
The reason the title of this review is ''Feelings'', is because the stories really get to your feelings and this was the main reason I kept playing this game.
When you've finally completed the game in 100%, which means playing all endings (believe me, it's worth it), you can download several mods and DLC which is a nice extra. I think this adds up to around 30 hours of gameplay, or if you're a fast reader, perhaps a bit less.
And the best part of it all,
I would've paid money to play this game, if I knew it was this good. It's great to see there are still awesome free games like this available.
All in all it's a great visual novel game with beautiful music, very interresting and emotional stories and best of all, it's free. Don't hesitate in trying out this game, it's worth it.

All of this while other people (or AI) are doing the same in the world around you, possibly influencing you positively or negatively in your quest for becoming the ultimate civilization and winning the game. If all of this sounds good to you, check this game out (I suggest doing so by using a sale to buy the game)!

I'd say this is a must buy for Hack&Slash/ARPG fans.
I find Grim dawn is more of an improved formula on Diablo 2 when compared to Diablo 3, in regards to the way skills and level up stats are applied atleast. You get pretty awesome freedom in your character build; Every level 3 skill points and 1 stat, your chosen class has its skill tree with a class mastery skill, so you need to level up this mastery to be able to invest in higher skills. When you reach level 10 its also possible to pick a second class which opens up that classes full skill line. You are also free to respec all your invested skill points at a npc, for some coin, but I dont think its possible to change a class though, and I was also unable to remove my points that were in my mastery skill.
Crafting is also a pretty important part in this, you can find blueprints for all kinds of gear that special blacksmith can forge for you. There are also various crafting materials that you will find that can be used on the enviroment that will open different paths and new areas. There are Dynamite around to that can be used to blow open heavy locked chests, break weakened walls, and you use them to dismantle gear to materials.
1 Thing Ive noticed here is there is no, or atleast less randonly generated areas, atleast I think the overworld stays the same layout, even between sessions, but the caves and attached areas are generated? I can't say for sure.
Also all gear pretty much has one 'socket' where you can insert a modifier piece for stats, you'll find this items in little pieces and once you have 3 or so they can be combined for a complete 'gem', the boosts this items give has a wide variety too which is awesome.
I'll also say this feels like its a much tougher game than other similar games I've played. Maybe my build just sucks lol, but I find the big mobs that are mixed with range/melee can really cut you down fast espcially if theres atleast one elite monster in the group with them. It keeps you on your toes though, and youll want to find cover from range and funnel in your melee through a doorway or something.
Can't say much about the story, I havent completed it yet, or really read much of the lore books. The setting is pretty cool though I think.
And as for Graphics go, I'd say Grim Dawn looks really good, very nice effects/ explosions , gibs. the lighting is pretty, and there is a day night cycle I think.
So there you go, don't even wait for a sale. Buy this game right now it's under 30$

An excellent remake of an old and treasured classic, with an innovative and new control system that keeps to the spirit of the original UFO game.
Turn based tactical combat where you are at a constant disadvantage against an opponent with greater numbers and better equipment, only your own decisions and the focused work of your research will allow you to face and eventually beat your alien opponent.
Enemy Within adds yet another layer to the overall tactics you need to employ with an all new enemy grouping and interesting new research venues to delve into, defending the planet from invasion has never been more fun.
If the regular game is too tame for your tastes there's the independent mod Long War to add more difficulty and danger to a game that already tries to beat you from the first minute of play, Long War changes the basic rules and research of the original game taking it one step closer to the brilliant game that started it all.
If you enjoy turn based tactical combat XCOM and it's mods will give you countless hours of fun at grief at the same  time.

This game is absolutely beautiful. The music is amazing, the asthetics are amazing, and overall I really love this game. And I haven't even played the full first hour of it, I only just reached Chapter 2 and it's already, without a doubt, one of my favourite games on my laptop.

Overall, I very very highly reccomend this game, especially if you like beautiful sound, beautiful asthetics, and fun mechanics.

HARDWARE: Win 10x64, i5 3570, GTX 1070. No slowdowns, no crashes. Initial lockups on loading screen that appear to be related to using Windows 10, but I was able to fix (see end of the review).
I was surprised to find I'm actually enjoying this game, given its harsh reviews, It's far from perfect, but it's also far from being a bad game at the current price point of $2.99. I'd probably be annoyed if I were expecting a AAA title and paid $50 for it, but it's fun despite a number of polish issues.
There was a major controversy surrounding this game and its developer's fight with a prominent Youtube reviewer in 2014. I have no dog in that fight, and it's not a consideration in my review.
The game:
- It has a good fictional premise: you're an alchemist hired to help stop a mysterious beast that has been attacking people in and near a castle, during the Middle Ages.
- The artwork is great, sort of a combination of cell-shading and 3D. It looks fairly primitive, but there is something about the style that tickles my fancy. I especially enjoyed the courtyard with falling snow.
- The music is evocative.
- It's fully voiced. The writing is generally good, with some obvious weak bits. The same goes for the voice acting.
- It does a good job keeping the plot moving.
The game isn't without its problems:
- It tries to install an unnecessary component (Ogg Vorbis) when you launch. I decline every time,
- Running in Windows 10 requires setting Windows 7 + Administrator compatibility modes on the game's executable file, or it freezes on the load screen.
- The game only supports auto-saves, done every time your journal updates. This means lost progress if you want to quit before hitting a new save point.
- You can't view the keybinds within the game.
- Advancing requires reading the manual, because it describes a couple of controls / features you are unlikely to figure out on your own, and they are necessary to understand or you'll get stuck VERY early. However, the manual spoils a couple of surprises that I think are better left to experiencing in-game. You can read my as-non-spoiler-as-possible hints instead:
- Some of the things you must do are fictionally illogical, such as
- Similarly illogical are the chests scattered about that you can (must?) pick.
- The map is useless, as it's just 2D sprites and doesn't show your position.
- NPC models and animations are pretty crude, though they get the job done.
- Puzzles are super simple, not much above walking simulator level (might be a positive depending on your preferences).
Most of the above are technical / polish issues that could be patched, though it seems unlikely they will be at this point. The underlying game is fundamentally sound, and an enjoyable experience with a little patience for its rough bits.
FIXING THE LOADING SCREEN FREEZE ON WINDOWS 10:
Setting Windows 7 and Administrator mode on the two game executables fixed it for me:
- RIGHT-click on Guise of the Wolf in in your list of games, and select PROPERTIES.
- Select the LOCAL FILES tab, then BROWSE LOCAL FILES
- Open the GAME folder
- Set the two Guise of the Wolf files to Windows 7 and Run as Administrator compatibility mode:
- RIGHT click and select PROPERTIES
- Select the COMPATIBILITY tab.
- Check the box to run in COMPATIBILITY MODE, and set it to Windows 7.
- Check the box to RUN AS ADMINISTRATOR.
- Click OK.

Originally released on arcades in Japan on April 30th 2015 with Playstation 3 and Playstation 4 releases on December 10th 2015 in Japan, February 2nd 2016 in North America and April 7th 2016 in Europe we have Nitro+ Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel. The version of the game being reviewed is the recent PC release of the game which came out on December the 8th 2016. Developed by Examu with Nitroplus and Marvelous publishing in Japan, and Marvelous and XSEED Games handling the game outside of Japan, the game is a sequel to Nitro Royale Heroines Duel; a Doujin game released back in 2009. For transparency, I received this game for free from a PR network.
Nitro+ Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel pits 14 characters against one another from Nitro+’s works as well as guest characters such as Homura from Marvelous’ Senran Kagura series, Aino Heart from Examu’s Arcana Heart series and Saber from Fate/Stay Night in her Fate/Zero appearance. As well as 14 characters, players can also pick 2 from 20 assist characters to aid them in battle with those characters coming from Nitro+’ works. Be aware if you do look further into some of the series the characters come from, they do contain some NSFW material and content that may offend. The main story of the game has the characters drawn in from their respective worlds to fight their way back home. But… Is the game any good? Find out in…
[THE GOOD]
While the story seems more like a standard Arcade mode where your character fights their way through a gauntlet of opponents and has an ending, I really liked the additional story content added after completing the game. Without spoiling too much, the additional story plays out like a visual novel with fights happening inbetween. It also allows you to play as different characters and learn their strengths and weaknesses. You also don’t need to know the characters or their backgrounds to understand what’s going on which makes it accessible to newcomers and veterans alike. The game also mentions which Nitro+ title to look into for more information which I found quite nice.
The range of characters I though was good. Each character has some pretty unique moves and a good range of attacks. On top of that they each have 21 different colours available with some acting as references too. Homura, Aino Heart and Super Sonico also have a swimsuit as an alternate costume as well. Character’s ultimate attacks are accompanied by an animation which adds its own sort of flair to the game. Support characters I found were useful and how you use them can also turn the tide of battle in your favour. But with all things good, there’s always…
[THE BAD]
User interface could do with a bit of work. If I were to accidentally select a character I didn’t want to play as, the game offers no back option. When the appropriate button is pressed, the game will request whether you want to go back to the main menu as opposed to cancelling the previous choice you had made. This can get very annoying, especially when you accidentally pick the wrong support character and have to go all the way back to the beginning again and select your main character again, just to pick the right support character.
Ironically coming from someone who edited Melty Blood stages in the fighting engine MUGEN, most of the in-game stages I thought were a little bland. In comparison to Nitro Royale Heroines Duel, the stages may visually look better, but I feel they’re empty and lack excitement. Maybe adding in background characters or more effects on some stages would have been a nice touch, but you would have to balance it out so the stages aren’t distracting the player in the middle of a fight. A couple of stages I’ll admit fit the atmosphere but asides form that, there really isn’t anything memorable to take away from it. Thankfully the character roster and their animations certainly make up for this. Asides from that, I can’t think of anything else, so it’s now time for…
[THE OPINION]
Nitro+ Blasterz: Heroines Infinite Duel is a solid fighting game with a story (or well, extra story) that was interesting enough to read. While it doesn’t seem to bring anything new to the table, I’ve found that even for someone who isn’t great at fighting games such as myself, it’s an easy game to pick up and adjust to. I do know a majority of the characters and support characters, but for newcomers, no prior knowledge about them is needed if you want to enjoy the game. However, for veterans, I don’t think the game will really scratch the itch but I would still play it for the enjoyment factor. Netplay was rather enjoyable and I never really had any issues with it despite my location being terrible for latency. Overall, I had a fun time playing the game and I can see myself coming back to it every so often to play it.

Nitroplus Blasterz is way, way more accessible than I expected it to be, and a lot of fun to pick up and play. Maybe my limited time with Guilty Gear and BlazBlue set up the assumption that "anime fighters are fun to watch, but have 500 different interlocking complex systems that make them utterly unplayable casually", but Blasterz seems... pretty straightforward? The core systems and commands seem pretty easy to wrap your head around, and It "looks" cool enough even early on that it's fun to play even if you're not dropping ultra-tourney level "tech".
The commands are the usual fireball and dragon punch motions and pretty common across characters, and there's only one charge meter to keep track of and it tends to work the same for everyone (powered up specials take up 1 out of 3 bar chunks, a dial-a-combo chain attack thingy for 2 chunks, or your ultra-mega-super-super for 3 chunks). You've got light/medium/heavy attacks like most fighting games, then a "guard" button for evasion and combo-breaking, and a "super heavy" button for pushing around and crushing through guard. You can whip out a "break out of any combo" thing once a round, and enter a fire-up mode as well that builds meter along with some other stuff as well. It's all... pretty easy to come to grips with?
While there's not that many characters, getting to pick 2 support characters adds some fun variety to things (a lot of them just seem like extra attacks at different ranges or heights, but others do wacky stuff like pop out powerups, or fill your meter). At least the game gives you a few "recommended" supports for each char too, which is nice.
I dunno, maybe it's just that i'm coming off the initial "oh god, this is impenetrable" impression from the last BlazBlue, or the new Street Fighter 5's disastrous launch of "we're going to introduce a bunch of new systems, but not actually teach you anything about any of them, or how to even use them", Blasterz seems refreshingly straightforward. It's just a lot of fun to play, even at a pretty casual level.

I am more than pleased with my download of this game. I enjoyed most of the characters and their paths. The music was well picked. The multiple endings were numerous.
When I look for a visual novel there are aspects I want.
1. Choices throughout the game:
these don't need to be giant factors in the game that need to effect end game. Just enough to change how a scene plays out. Everlasting Summer score 9/10
2. Multiple endings:
I enjoy a replay value. I like a good ending and a bad ending and more important a vastly different ending. Score 9/10
3. Animation and CG:
I want things polished more than I want things to just exist in the game. Ideally I want pretty graphics and CG scenes (possibly interactive). Everlasting summer 6.5/10. This was the weakest point for the game and i'm surprised with such a small company and staff it wasn't worse. Even more, I was happy with what I got. I still have a full gallery and unique art that you wont find in the j visual novels.
4. Music:
The music is extremely important and has to be appropriate. If you dont understand, try watching Star Wars footage without the music. If the music isn't appropriate, it kills the mood and the attachment to the world. 9/10 There's a large library of music listed. I just wish there was a little more unique and flushed music with Alisa's route.
5. Story/Writing:
It's a visual novel. A novel can't be good without story and writting, simple as that. 8/10. I felt cheated with a route where I follow a voice and then zero explaination (I assumed I died?). A couple other hic ups here and there. The character can really just go off into a monolgue. The writing also had a lot of allusions to other works and pop culture which i enjoyed for the most part. It was also written well enough for me to play through every route. I can't say it's on the level of writing like Critical Point (the writers from UC gundam worked on that visual novel), but it's a great start.
Overall 8/10. It was for the most part what I wanted. And that doesn't factor that this game was free. These ratings have no pulled punches as this was a professional quality of work. I look forward to the next one: Love, Money, Rock'n'Roll.

A tactical roleplaying game with a norse mythology theme created by Stoic (which I believe is just three men who used to work for BioWare). The story has tonnes of Lore if you look around the map, but if you want the basics of the story then the return or a warlike race that despises humanity - The Dredge - led by an invincible leader called Bellower has sent the world into chaos.
The gameplay is a strategical, turn-based sing-player combat against the Dredge or other survivors and each character in your caravan has certain skills and unique abilities that can help you develop solid stratedgies for taking down opponents. It has the novel idea of your health also representing strength, so the more health you lose the less powerful your character's attacks will be. You have a whole array of units such as archers, shieldbangers, warhawks, etc.
Inbetween battles there are chapters, in each chapter you will play as one of three POV characters leading a caravan across this hostile world in a way similar to "Oregon Trail". Here you will make conversation choices with other characters and sometimes the wrong ones will result in your characters dying or leaving for good, which results in you having less units to fight with in the tactical combat - a lot of people have a problem with this but it actually works as good incentive to level up everyone rather than just focus on one character and make them the best; you could lose them at any point. One character in particular, Egil, who has a special ability that let's him block almost any attack (so pretty useful when utilised correctly) can be killed about 8 times during these conversation choices and you actually get an achievement for keeping him alive! The choices also offer a bit of replayability in terms of characters but there is little in the way of overall change.
The game isn't perfect; in the "Oregon Trail" part you have fighters, clansmen and varl (Varl are part of the mythology and are giants with horns) that you are charged with keeping alive, managing supplies to do so, but many players point out you can let them all starve to death and still complete the game without consequences, however it seems this will remedied in the sequel which will make your caravan more important.
Another issue is that there is little difference in terms of combat scenarios with everyone with the terrain remaining basically the same and the enemies changing only slightly over the course of the game, due to the different number of units you have to experiment with the game rarely gets boring or too repetitive but given it's estimated run time of about 8 hours you're unlikely to get tired of it in that time.
A lot of people take issue with the game opening with a cinematic scene and not having any more in the game and their is little voice-acting. But if you judge this game by that then you are missing out. The artwork is beautiful and it is well written if a few of the in-universe words (such as the insult "Skal") can take a while to understand.
Ultimatley, the game has its little imperfections, but they don't take away from this being a spectacular and original game that is definitley worth playing. A fun experience that is excellently presented and executed with a diverse cast of characters, intricate and compelling story and a solid combat system.

This game is delightful and remains my favorite game on Steam. It's also my favorite party game. I haven't uninstalled it since I bought the game, and it has been months. The gameplay kicks butt and is incredibly fun, the monsters and traps are delightful, and you can clock hours of play on it.  One thing I really appretiated was the very balanced system. The most levels that your opponents get as a human, the stronger your monsters get, as you collect spendable Wrath points from each of their levels. This ensures that, if one player is especially dominating as the human, the weakest player is allowed to catch up by giving them the strongest monster advantage, without weakening the other players.  The most recent add-on of scrolls has also been incredibly good, allowing you to steal items from other players. Items like these ensure that even the strongest players are not 100% safe and means that there is always a chance at redemption. This is a great game!
P.S. Most people complain about there being no online capability. Personally, I prefer gaming on the couch, with friends. This game is also compatible with USB replica SNES and NES controllers, which are great for that classic experience.

Barrels of fun. Fun on a bun. Bun bun fun fun barrel with friends.
Practice with the bots, and then invite your friends over to crush them until they catch up.
Or spend time analyzing the game to take down your friends strategically:
At the beginning of the game, the human character is far more powerful than the monsters. The monsters have to run, hide, and perform various shenanigans. Without good strategy, the monsters get killed and the human character can get super far ahead at the beginning. But as a direct response to the human character getting ahead, the monsters become stronger. The balance shifts to the reverse; the monsters are now the powerful ones, and the human character now has to be more creative, and inevitably, they will succumb to the gradual loss of health that is the life of a rogue-liker. Now, a less powerful human player takes the wheel, and they will most likely get killed by the most powerful monster (the weakest human player), gradually balancing the game while leaning towards the more skilled players.
There are two things that are wrong with this. One is that there is exactly one strategy that works at a certain given time; you either run and hide, or charge relentlessly, and it has an obvious curve; the less powerful you are, the more sneaky you should be. No other strategy will lead you to success.
Another is that it isn't always the most powerful monster that kills the player; sometimes, like in other games, there are people who sneak in for the last hit without doing much of the damage at all. This means that the one that camps far away and sneaks in a blow when the player is at low health is the one that gets the reward.
Therefore, in order to kill the human and become the human (which gives you the lead), you have to stay behind the lines of other monsters until the human is at low health, at which point you act according to your level of power; if you're powerful, charge right at them to get the last hit in, and if you're a lower level monster, shoot at them with everything you have while staying out of the line of fire.
The meta can be advanced from here, but this is all you need to invite your friends over and crush them until they catch up.
More meta - The killing blow is the killing blow, no matter how small. This means that quantity over quality is what you want for your monsters. Anything with damage-over-time effects will be more likely to get you human status.
It's also not a good idea to kill the human early on - there are still lots of other monsters; you'll be cannon fodder. Wait for someone else to take the bait and then reap.
Now invite your friends over, so that you can crush them. Then you should make a lot of tables and graphs, and then invite your friends over, so that you can crush them.
Point and laugh at your family as they struggle helplessly to kill your ever-stronger player character. Erupt in anger when your own friends kill you in an epic boss fight. On a bun. Fun on a bun in a bindle barrel bun with friends on a bun with the fun of a barrel of bindle bun fun with friends.
Buy this game.

Crawling through dungeon, haunted by the ghosts of friends you slayed in cold blood sounds like a horror game... but this is pretty much a monster filled Mario Party so the real conflict is trying to not ACTUALLY slay your friends in cold blood.
You start off with you and however many players you're playing against in a room. NOW FIGHT! Starting off, everyone is a one shot kill, so these few delicate moments could change the tide of the entire game. So, being the last one alive means you're the first one to roam the dungeon.
Everyone else follows you as a ghost. These ghost can spawn monsters, set off traps, and throw furniture at you. Playing as the ghosts is one of the more fun parts of the game, but fighting the monsters and staying one step ahead of your friends as the hero, is just as fun.
Health is rare and expensive when found in stores, so every drop of health counts, making it all the more devastating when your friends kill you with a crate... But, it's all in good fun... Right? RIGHT?!
The upgrade system is fun. The stronger the hero gets, the stronger he plays, but the stronger the hero gets, the more powerful all of the ghosts get. This power can be used to upgrade the monsters. Also, I gotta love the simplistic weapon system that just tells you if it's better or not, without having to pull out a calculator. Oh, the spells are also pretty cool, though some seem a bit unbalanced, this seems intentional and I love it.
Oh! And the fact that little orbs the ghosts collect go all around the room and the orbs can be used to spawn slimes! It's fun and a great time waster while the hero changes weapons in the shop.
I also like how every time you beat the game you unlock evolutions for monsters, or new sets to start off with. It's reminiscent of Pokemon and I always want to see what new monstrosities I get to kill my friends with!
My biggest problem in this game is that it truly takes competitive people to play the way it's meant to be played. You have to truly want to kill the hero, which leads to some problems for some of your friends who might just want to help you. So, maybe add in some sort of All Players VS AI mode?
You might have noticed that I've basically only talked about playing this with friends, there is AI to play against, but this is the kind of game that is truly meant to be played with friends, which is why I don't have many hours on it... *insert crying*
Also, online multiplayer... Get on it.

In my opinion, this was an excellent visual novel. The graphics were beautiful, the soundtrack was great (literally moved me to tears sometimes, some of the songs gave me chills they were so emotional and beautiful). The plot was pretty good, too. Yes the plot had some holes in it, but that can be expected from their first game. Overall, this was a great visual novel. If you like visual novels, like multiple-outcome games, or are just curious about this game, get it! It's free. FREE! I mean, it wouldn't hurt to at least try it. Also, if you're looking for a game with a lot of boobs or panty-shots, don't bother, it's not (entirely) like that. Even though there are a few panty-shot, low tops, and a few sex scenes (which are blocked out of course), this isn't a game entirley based around getting a girl, banging her, and living "happily ever after" in La-la land. It's about an average guy, falling asleep on a bus in Winter, waking up to a Summer pioneer camp in the 80's, and maybe even find love, all the while trying to figure out why and how he's there. So in summary, buy the game. It's well made and enjoyable.

This is a fun but repetitive little sports/shooter game with a few cool game modes. It's definitely a nice time-killer if you want to get in a couple of quick games of something without much fuss or learning curve. *However*, there are three big flaws that keep me from giving this game a positive recommendation. 1)  The online community is absolutely bare, so online multiplayer matches are filled with bots to make up the numbers. 2) The graphics are simple, which is cool, but the use of simple shapes + neon lighting + constant movement is disorienting and headache-inducing. Playing the game for more than a few matches is really uncomfortable. This might be just me, to be fair, but it's something to think about if you tend to get nauseous from first-person games. 3) Finally, the asking price is waaaay too high. If you want to try out the game, wait for a deep sale - a couple of bucks at most - before you shell out your cash. 10 dollars is way, way too much for this, in my opinion. It's too repetitive and simple to warrant the price tag, and it's not like you're joining in on a thriving game community. If you've got a bunch of online friends to play with or your gaming group likes to play local multiplayer matches around your computer, that might give the game a bit more value for you...but even then, it's not worth full price.

You’re start out in a random country side and your carriage gets attacked by some unknown creature. You wake up in the middle of a wintery forest area and start to look for your carriage driver. You eventually venture into the abandon castle to find out you’ve been bitten. As it turns out the Lord of the castle called upon you to create a cure for this curse that plagues the castle.
The story is so so. It slowly draws you in and will put many to sleep at the same time. It gives little to no character development and still leaves holes in the story even at the end. For a ‘horror’ based game there is very little horror to the story seeing as it’s either laughably bad or easily defeated. They did take some unique turns in making a monster story, like making potions and cures. But it ends slightly cliché, even with two different endings. Don’t get me wrong the endings are nicely done, but you’ve probably seen them before.
The graphics are terribly dated, but that’s nothing new with Indy games. Even with dated graphics many have found a way to make them artistic looking or add some different qualities to enhance their limitations. One good example is Papers, Please. It’s a very stressful take on living in a 3rd world country as a boarder security guard. The graphs are utter crap. However shading and simple design help bring the game to a very dreary vivid world. With Guise Of The Wolf it very much reminds me of Theif 2, except it lacks most things. In many areas where a shadow would be cast on someone it shows them in regular lighting. Also many of the characters appear to be BRIGHTER then the surrounding area for some reason. Then when I’d load the game again it would do a 180 and show the complete opposite of what I stated above. Another thing that stand out is that many of the characters have very very limited movement. The guards of the castle seem to have 3, a women you meet in the kitchen seems to only have 2, and the main bad guy only has 4. Now sure it would be different if they were 2d, but this is a 3d world that would probably be a few more hours of coding to be a little lusher and it drains away from the submersion aspect of video games all together. To a certain extent the graphics set back the experience all together.
The controls are wonky to say the least. They start out smooth, but it seems there are too many unfinished parts of the game. So despite how many times you smash down a button it becomes more and more difficult to wiggle out of a glitch in a piece of scenery. Many times I found myself falling through the world or I would get stuck on invisible pieces of something that would render all the controls moot. Other times I would hit a button to perform a action and it just didn’t work. Like say if I wanted to take something. It wouldn’t grasp a clearly graspable object, but when I hit the same button seconds later it would pick up that same object.
In the end this was just a bad game. It was a good attempt for a indy developer. However due to the graphics and story it would have probably been higher rated if it was released years ago and put more time into it. With dated PlayStation 1 like graphics and bland story I can’t recommend it, but can’t say you shouldn’t avoid it either. Although I will say the things that they did well, like some of the voice acting, doesn’t do enough to redeem it completely. However for the more ADD ridden gamer they’ll find themselves bored and frustrated. So if you can get it for cheap buy it. It’s worth a few hours if your really bored. Unfortunately in the end it’s easily forgettable and a mildly regrettable experience.

For all the obvious reasons, anyone who's a fan of this series should know this rule anyways right?
Speaking of which, I would recommend this mainly to fans primarily to the TV series who are caught up or willing to face spoilers and maybe if they're fans of the books. I prefer the books because I'm a sucker for details and the player is granted extra information to read up on within the 'codex' in the main menu. While you are able to make choices you will in no way impact the actual storyline (like killing Joffery way earlier or something).
I will admit that this was my first time actually playing a Telltale game rather than watching friends play them and I gotta say, it was stressful in all the good ways. I definitely immersed myself into the game and was able to sympathize easily with the characters and my reactions ended up on par with many of the characters too. This was fantastic use of emotion in levels on the developers’ part! Obviously it would have been even more immersion if I was able to create my own little lord and lady from scratch but that's not how that world works in the first place (they would probably die anyways).
The gameplay was weird and the tutorial was totally incomplete. I understood the click, hold, drag mechanic easily but didn't know that the arrows meant to press the arrow keys/ wasd keys at all! Dunno if I just overlooked it but when I looked it up once I had gotten stuck trying to click and drag for 5 minutes, it had turned out that others were having the same problem... Once you get the hang of things though, prepare to very slightly sit back and definitely enjoy the game.
With making choices I felt torn between my own morals and the characters morals. I understand that you have the choice to say whatever you want but there is no way you can tell the outcome of your dialogue without chance or having previous knowledge of the character(s) you're talking to. Of course, the entire Forrester house doesn't count because there has never been any information on them before. So if you understand how the characters are and can play to them you're likely to succeed in getting the response you want.
Except for Ramsay Snow. Dear god he terrifies me... Much more in the books since a minds imagination when it comes to villians is much worse than reality, but having to face his brutality in first-person view isn't exactly a pleasant feeling.
Due to the brutality that this world will unleash upon humanity relentlessly, this game has a major shock factor just waiting for us all.

XCOM has a long history of being the daddy of turn based strategic games and with good reason.  every revision of the game is playable to the extreme and customizable to a certain degree with the sheer number of options available to you with squad formation and skills.
Its not a game without its faults, in as much as the games legendary difficulty will no doubt testify to, and that missed shot, that squad member who dies and that enemy that just wont go down will all accumulate to have you pulling your hair out in frustration, but there's a sadistic pleasure in that because this game is literally different every time you play it.  Shots don't always land and things don't always go your way, just like in real life.
With the addition of the "XCOM:  Enemy Within" DLC, yet another faction is added to the game and helps to break up the monotony of missions with some new challenges, but ultimately, its the same game and there isn't enough there to make me want to replay it too often.  What would have been nice is to add a map tool to make your own arenas and be able to play the aliens as well as the humans.  An online challenge mode with multiplayer gaming would add years of enjoyment to this, but since the game is now a pretty much dead IP and any further development will be in a new game, but for those who are interested, I would check out the Mod scene.  the game is based on the Unreal engine, therefore there's lots of people out there that are modding away making stuff for this and other unreal based games.  (NexusMods for instance has PAGES of stuff for XCOM)
It may not be perfect, but I think this stands as a testimony to the turn based strategy game at its finest and most annoying.  A single campaign will take you the best part of a week and for the occasional time killer, this is a great cheap game.  definitely worth a look see!

Hello prospective XCOM commanders. I would like to say future commanders because this is a very excellent turn-based strategy game. Simply put, you control a squad of elite soldiers against an alien invasion. Early on, you don't have many resources, the aliens are flat-out stronger than you. Later on, you can fight the aliens on equal ground.
If you do plan on dunking 30 bones on this title, which I do recommend, strategic pro tip: Make sure that you are making satellites all the time, as well as sufficient uplink. Only launch satellites at the end of each in-game month. Trust me. And a tactical pro tip: Always use cover and Overwatch. As in Overwatch on EVERY TURN. EDIT: On hard difficulties, hunkering behind high cover is better. 80% chance for aliens to whiff shots? Yes please!
Also, get used to the prospect of permanent death. If your soldiers die, they RIP forever. (Unless you reload.) Whoops, forgot one more pro tip: Always play Ironman mode or don't reload saves to avert deaths. If you're going to play this game, you've gotta man up.
TL;DR: Excellent game, and actually challenging. (You won't find this game to be a snoozefest.) 9.5/10.

A tactical roleplaying game with a norse mythology theme created by Stoic (which I believe is just three men who used to work for BioWare). The story has tonnes of Lore if you look around the map, but if you want the basics of the story then the return or a warlike race that despises humanity - The Dredge - led by an invincible leader called Bellower has sent the world into chaos.
The gameplay is a strategical, turn-based sing-player combat against the Dredge or other survivors and each character in your caravan has certain skills and unique abilities that can help you develop solid stratedgies for taking down opponents. It has the novel idea of your health also representing strength, so the more health you lose the less powerful your character's attacks will be. You have a whole array of units such as archers, shieldbangers, warhawks, etc.
Inbetween battles there are chapters, in each chapter you will play as one of three POV characters leading a caravan across this hostile world in a way similar to "Oregon Trail". Here you will make conversation choices with other characters and sometimes the wrong ones will result in your characters dying or leaving for good, which results in you having less units to fight with in the tactical combat - a lot of people have a problem with this but it actually works as good incentive to level up everyone rather than just focus on one character and make them the best; you could lose them at any point. One character in particular, Egil, who has a special ability that let's him block almost any attack (so pretty useful when utilised correctly) can be killed about 8 times during these conversation choices and you actually get an achievement for keeping him alive! The choices also offer a bit of replayability in terms of characters but there is little in the way of overall change.
The game isn't perfect; in the "Oregon Trail" part you have fighters, clansmen and varl (Varl are part of the mythology and are giants with horns) that you are charged with keeping alive, managing supplies to do so, but many players point out you can let them all starve to death and still complete the game without consequences, however it seems this will remedied in the sequel which will make your caravan more important.
Another issue is that there is little difference in terms of combat scenarios with everyone with the terrain remaining basically the same and the enemies changing only slightly over the course of the game, due to the different number of units you have to experiment with the game rarely gets boring or too repetitive but given it's estimated run time of about 8 hours you're unlikely to get tired of it in that time.
A lot of people take issue with the game opening with a cinematic scene and not having any more in the game and their is little voice-acting. But if you judge this game by that then you are missing out. The artwork is beautiful and it is well written if a few of the in-universe words (such as the insult "Skal") can take a while to understand.
Ultimatley, the game has its little imperfections, but they don't take away from this being a spectacular and original game that is definitley worth playing. A fun experience that is excellently presented and executed with a diverse cast of characters, intricate and compelling story and a solid combat system.

Do you feel like playing an RPG that can punish or reward you for every single moral decision you ever make? Are you prepared to redefine what you consider "moral" as your mental and strategic mettle are put the the test constantly? And finally, can you handle the emotional consequences of your actions as you struggle to balance the needs of keeping yourself, your party, and the rest of your caravan alive?
Banner Saga puts the questions to the test as you traverse through a gorgeous, norse mythological world...albeit on the run from dire enemies all the while. The game is fantastic overall, despite the rather monotonous and somewhat flawed battling system (e.g., an odd turn-based system that alternates your turn and the enemies every time; thus, even if you have 6 members alive and they have only 2, they still get to go multiple times while your characters only get to go once in turn). However, the real appeal is essentially the entire story itself: It is full of twists and turns, celebrations and mourning, and heart-wrenching choices through every step along the way. And the music! Oh, the music is simply some of the most aesthetically pleasing sounds you will ever hear; fitting seamlessly throughout the gameplay.
This game is only part one of several (out of a total of three I believe that are in development), so pick it up now while you have the chance (and when it is on sale of course!). I believe this game cuts a well-earned 9 Varl (Viking) axes out of 10 Dredge heads. If you have any questions for me about the game, please leave a comment on this review and I will be happy to try to answer them.

Yeah, that was a surprise.
There are plenty of hidden gems out there on Steam, but I did NOT expect this game to be this good. At all. And here I am, writing a glowing review for a visual novel, of all things.
Everlasting Summer is... well, what exactly IS Everlasting Summer? It's free. It's surprisingly complex. It has a cast of likeable characters. It has above-par writing. The artwork is beautiful to look at. And it's all around a pleasant experience, that left me smiling at the end.
Without spoiling anything, the game focuses on a protagonist that is a lifeless loser and spends all his time online... sound familiar, anyone? He eventually embarks on a bus to be transported to a surreal summer camp filled with five various sexual fantasies for him to either take advantage of or properly learn and establish a relationship with. And it's your choices that also define his personality for that particular game, as well as his relationships with the other characters. It may seem like a simple dating sim, but the world of Everlasting Summer carries a deep, dark undertone that shows just how fake the world of Camp Slovyonok and how much dark, disturbing imagery is lying just underneath it.
Is there sex in the game? Yes. But it's not the main focus. If you wish to pursue a girl, you have to show interest in her and learn more about her while also learning more about the world you live in simultaneously, and even after the sex comes the aftereffects, where you learn your good/bad consequences for what you've done and what their impact is on you.
Ironically, "Everlasting Summer" is both a title that conveys happy thoughts but dark ones as well. Almost as if Semyon is constantly trapped in an Everlasting Summer, and can't seem to find his way out, until you- the player- decides to find his ending outside of the game. It's that subtle meta-narrative that really took this game up a notch for me.
Does this game have its problems? Of course it does. Certain portions feel like crossing off a checklist, the final achievement in a massive pain to complete, and the Yulya ending is a bit lackluster. But this game will end up grabbing your interest, even if you don't like visual novels. It's a good story with good characters, and a complex world that'll keep you guessing and theorizing every time you find one of Everlasting Summer's many endings. It's like digging around in the dirt to find a massive maze that you just want to keep exploring and find every single nook and cranny. A high recommendation for anyone with absolutely no money who wants to try something very new.

As a veteran player of aRPGs, I want to share my feels about Grim Dawn with you, after about 90h of gameplay.
Features I like:
+ Involving, dark story.
+ Beautiful graphics and style,
+ Atmospheric soundtrack,
+ Very satisfying and 'meaty' combat model,
+ Faction system with bounties and nemezis hunting (though I've never faced any),
+ Devotion system,
+ Festival of loot,
+ Good crafting system,
+ Lots of components, aguments and item-granted skills which provide wide variety of builds,
+ Day/night and wheater system,
+ At some point it's quite challenging (over 70 deaths druing 90h of gameplay),
+ I haven't try multiplayer yet, but I am sure it's very, very fun (instanced or FFA loot, combat with friends, etc.),
+ Easy, reasonable travel system,
+ Vast locations filled with details and less linear than in most aRPGs,
+ Lots of hidden treasuers, places and secret quests,
+ Possibility to rotate and zoom camera and map,
+ Modding tools with huge possibilites,
+ Class dualism..
+ .. but it would be awesome to add new classes (TQ:IT had 9). However, it's definitely great with 6 various classes at the moment.
+ One of the best price/quality deals,
+ Hardcore mode.
Features I'm neutral about:
* Consistent world - I couldn't feel Cairn division into acts,
* Lack of character customization (only male/female - same as TQ),
* Absence of shrines with buffs (present in TQ), however I think they're not necessary here,
* I have a problem with memorizing locations, NPCs and major bosses names,
* Lack of Polish language,
* After 90h of gameplay my character is at lvl.. 78/85.
* After creating new character it doesn't show up instantly - player must go to options and come back to main menu to see it.
Things I dislike:
- Aetherfire (green flame on the ground) and poison pools are bit overpowered,
- Few animations should be improved (e.g. stonetusks),
- Sometimes vision gets too dark,
- Ocassionaly crashes at alt-tabbing or game exiting.
Incoming first DLC - Crucible - is a hope for a better endgame content with a chance for ranking rivalry and source of loot (hopefully also new).
I believe that future content will make this game one of the best aRPG's of all time (for me it is now).
A must have - not only for aRPG genre lovers!

Overall, the game is good, but it is not without it's flaws
Cons:
-The game's controller support is very lacking requiring you to take control of the mouse in the game to interact with characters and menus. Support seems to have been an afterthought.
-The components in the game are stackable, but due to the fact that merging components creates different components, they do not stack by default, making inventory management a hassle.
-The opening cutscene is great but you will not find these throughout most of the game. some voice acted dialogue is all you should expect
-Somehow, me and my friend ended up friendly with opposing factions while playing with each other - making traversing their territories awkward and more challenging.
-The menus are not intuitive, and lack in-game explanation. Ability descriptions start with mostly lore and flavor and it is difficult to tell what they actually do.
-Some classes seem to far exceed others in capability
Pros:
-The gameplay is fun
-The levelling/talent system paired with the devotion system makes for very fulfilling progression.
-There is an expansive world with varying terrain to explore.
-Equipment is varied and interesting
-Portals! They make it easy to play with other people, and even incentivises multiplayer, because if you die, you can jump right back into battle if your cohort is alive.

XCOM has a long history of being the daddy of turn based strategic games and with good reason.  every revision of the game is playable to the extreme and customizable to a certain degree with the sheer number of options available to you with squad formation and skills.
Its not a game without its faults, in as much as the games legendary difficulty will no doubt testify to, and that missed shot, that squad member who dies and that enemy that just wont go down will all accumulate to have you pulling your hair out in frustration, but there's a sadistic pleasure in that because this game is literally different every time you play it.  Shots don't always land and things don't always go your way, just like in real life.
With the addition of the "XCOM:  Enemy Within" DLC, yet another faction is added to the game and helps to break up the monotony of missions with some new challenges, but ultimately, its the same game and there isn't enough there to make me want to replay it too often.  What would have been nice is to add a map tool to make your own arenas and be able to play the aliens as well as the humans.  An online challenge mode with multiplayer gaming would add years of enjoyment to this, but since the game is now a pretty much dead IP and any further development will be in a new game, but for those who are interested, I would check out the Mod scene.  the game is based on the Unreal engine, therefore there's lots of people out there that are modding away making stuff for this and other unreal based games.  (NexusMods for instance has PAGES of stuff for XCOM)
It may not be perfect, but I think this stands as a testimony to the turn based strategy game at its finest and most annoying.  A single campaign will take you the best part of a week and for the occasional time killer, this is a great cheap game.  definitely worth a look see!

I absolutely recommend "Child of Light".
Before you consider playing this game, please keep in mind the fact that this is a fairy tale. Virtually all of the characters speak in rhymes and the art style has a dream-like quality to it. If you are expecting a typical JRPG, this game may disappoint you.
While I am not a huge JRPG fan, the battle system work and as a few quirks to it. At the bottom of the screen, you can see everybody moving along the "Wait" bar. At the end of the "Wait" Bar is the "Cast" bar. Each skill has a difference casting length. You are able to interrupt an enemy that is casting a long spell or ability and they are able to interupt you! Additionally, your "firefly" companion Igniculus is able to heal characters in battle and slow down enemy turns.
PROS:
- Great music.
- Beautiful art style. This game is like playing a painting.
- Charming characters.
- New Game+.
CONS:
- UPlay is required. I had only one minor issue with it, but I have heard that others have had some extreme difficulty with UPlay.
- Short. I finished it in about 8 hours (I completed all but two sidequests).
- You are only allowed two characters in a battle. Considering that you can face up to 3 enemies at a time and the large number of party members you acquire, I wish you could have three characters per battle.

Hello prospective XCOM commanders. I would like to say future commanders because this is a very excellent turn-based strategy game. Simply put, you control a squad of elite soldiers against an alien invasion. Early on, you don't have many resources, the aliens are flat-out stronger than you. Later on, you can fight the aliens on equal ground.
If you do plan on dunking 30 bones on this title, which I do recommend, strategic pro tip: Make sure that you are making satellites all the time, as well as sufficient uplink. Only launch satellites at the end of each in-game month. Trust me. And a tactical pro tip: Always use cover and Overwatch. As in Overwatch on EVERY TURN. EDIT: On hard difficulties, hunkering behind high cover is better. 80% chance for aliens to whiff shots? Yes please!
Also, get used to the prospect of permanent death. If your soldiers die, they RIP forever. (Unless you reload.) Whoops, forgot one more pro tip: Always play Ironman mode or don't reload saves to avert deaths. If you're going to play this game, you've gotta man up.
TL;DR: Excellent game, and actually challenging. (You won't find this game to be a snoozefest.) 9.5/10.

A game with a fantastic and whimsical start full of fantasy and promise ends up pittering out in the end with a rushed ending and a lack of what it held so strongly in the beginning.
I loved the start of this game. It had me entranced so fully and I was sucked into it at once. The music is lovely and the art is something special. The drawn world with the 3d girl. It's beyond lovely. It's beautiful. The fairy tale like beginning of a little girl who is in this magical world. I was truly in love.
The game play is clean with its little faults here and there and the combat is simple. There is room for thought and cleverness when you fight  or you can just push your way through every battle.
About half way through I feel the game starts to lose a lot of it's charm. A little after you meet Aurua's sister is where I feel the magic starts to fade away. The story teller speaks to you for the last time till the end of the game and it's where you lose your sister as a party member that the magic just seems to fade away. And by the end it's just gone.
It's a rushed ending with a final boss just thrown at you with no build up. It just happens. And it ends about as fast as that. Your little child of light spends half the game not being a child and certainly doesn't end being a child. The issue with her father feels empty and forgotten. And Umbra, your big bad, feels uneventfull and not really that much of an issue.
Understandably this is not a big game and there is only room for what there is room for. But I feel, despite that, the ending shouldn't have been what it was. The story, to me, is just as important as everything else and when you fall so terribly short it's disappointing though I do not regret any money or time spent on the game. It was pretty and good for what it was, even with the lack luster ending.
It's said this game is boring, though I can see how one might feel that way, I do not find it so. It's a typical rpg with talking. You walk some your characters stop and talk. You fight a couple battles your characters stop and talk. That's just familiar ground to me. The story itself is simple, perhaps boring? I found it enchanting. I suppose if you like whimsical and fanciful fairy tale like stories this would be a game for you, otherwise, perhaps not. For all it's faults and troublesome little issues it's a pretty game with a strong story start and a faltering end. Worth a single  playthrough and the few dollars it costs when it is on sale.
