I've been playing games for a long time. I rarely write reviews.
But Banner Saga deserves it.
I purchased this game on sale for five bucks and expected a gimmick. I expected an "indie" experience with nothing more to offer than unique visuals that would eventually get old. Really, I was kind of jaded from my past mistakes. Undertale, Child of light, the blind forest... yeah, you get the idea. They're aesthetic in their own right, but when you get right down to it, they suck. Empty cases of games that live off of being nothing more than a one trick pony. And to be honest, my opinion has some merit. I've been gaming for almost 30 yrs, so I'm past the point of caring what people think of me when I say such things. It's the truth, and it has value. Take it or leave it. So please listen when I say The Banner Saga, it ISN'T one of those games. It was my pleasurable surprise of the year.
Without spoiling too much of the game, I'll say that reviewers didn't accurately portray what this game was, at least in my experience. What I experienced in-game was completely different that what I was expecting according to reviews. Mechanically, it's essentially the oregon trail with Heroes III combat. If you enjoyed those two in school during childhood, you're in for a treat. You travel across a map for the sake of a story, and lead a caravan of a couple hundred people who you must make decisions for along the way. And the story, let me tell you, is amazeballs. Except for the end.
Which brings me to the only gripe of the game.
The story, the visuals, the gameplay, it's all great. Like I said, reminiscent of the oregon trail and HOMM III. But for some reason, at the end of the game (without giving away spoilers), the developers decided to make a certain combat sequence incredibly difficult. It's a design choice. And this isn't some subjective opinion. Everyone who has completed the game knows exactly what I'm talking about.  It can take up to twenty play throughs to "beat" it.
Now, that wouldn't be a problem if Banner Saga wasn't the game that it was. If it was a dark souls, or a TMNT cartridge fighting game from 1994, we'd be swell. But for me, the banner saga's beauty lied in the adventure. It's splendor revealed in it's journey. You make decisions that come from nowhere, and they affect your entire caravan. People die because of your choices but there's nothing you can do. You do the best you can, and you push on. You keep going. You get TOTALLY immersed. You're on a mission, and choices are made, and you hope for the best. But there's nothing you can do for the past. You really start to feel like you're on a journey of epic proportions. You really get suckered in to thinking it's real. You make decisions that you live with, good or bad, and you push on. That's the best way to describe banner saga. Until the end.
Because you'll die at the end. A lot.
Why? I can't imagine why the developers (they are ex-bioware emplyees, which speaks to the quality of the game) made this decision at the end, but they did. I lived with it, and it's still a GREAT game. Maybe they knew it was so similar to the oregon trail that they decided to pay homage to it and make the end scene incredibly difficult, reminiscent of the rafting at the end of oregon trail. I don't know.
So yes, the immersion get's broken a little by the frustration, but it's worth it. Buy the banner saga. The sequal is coming, and I have a feeling, being the developers they are, that banner saga 2 will only be improved. You'll love it. Surprise of 2016 for me, and I'm a 30 yr old gamer who realizes it's only April.

Before I begin, i have played this game multiple times from the closed alphas, closed beta, and even played on release. This is my 4th time redownloading and playing this game
I don't think this game is a bad game; visually its spectacular, the combat system is engaging and enjoyable, the character creaton system is on point.
This game definitely stands out compared to other MMO's and for the 6$ i spent on it while it was on sale (10$ is the regular price which is still very cheap) this game offers alot of different things compared to other really popular MMO's Like WoW and FF14.
The issues i have with this game is that for a game that offers all these spectacular features, i feel like the game may be too open than other MMO's. The world of the game is graphically appealing, but most of your time will be spent walking, or riding back and forth between towns and from town to town the appearance feels the same.
Much like any MMO it does offer a party and guild system, but unlike other MMO's the game doesn't feel very social, which for me is important as the 4 times ive redownloaded and played this game i did it at the request of friends.
The game offers players the option to run the game while doing actions while AFK like fishing. This is a nice feature, but i feel like it takes away from the enjoyment of actually playing the game.
The game also pulls you towards a repetitive grindfest, which isnt unlike other MMO's but the rewards for grinding on monsters and dungeons are lacking considering the most rewards are earned in the PvP. i dont have an issue with PvP existing but for myself i am not a big fan of it, for other players it can be what they like most about a game.
I think this is a great game but it just isn't a game for me; i feel like i can do most of the same things this game offers but i enjoy it in other games. If this game appeals to you because of its combat system, graphics, character customization, market system, and all the other aspects then by all means buy it because for the price you wont find another MMO like it.
I only leave my negative review because for the 4th time of redownloading and playing, i havent been able to find a reason to keep playing.

Starting off I really loved what FTL offered. The ability to manage your own space ship with your own mix crew exploring various sectors for rewards and dangers. Recruiting new crew members, adding weaponry and tech to your ship. As a lover of sci-fi, I really enjoyed this sense of immersion, and customization, but sadly this ended quickly.
It starts off at the beginning of the game. You are given a bare esstenial ship, but you are being chased by a rebel fleet equipped with weapons and tech that would rip you apart in a dog fight so you are forced to retreat. The fleet following you with every jump you make. To boost your ship and weaponry you have to explore the various sectors, but at the same time attempt to be ahead of the rebel fleet chasing you.
Now some may enjoy this sense of tension as you attempt to explore as much as you can before being caught but really it forces you to fly through the sector negating the purpose of exploring compound with the fact the sectors get harder and harder as you progress. To which by the time you get to the end you are faced against a boss that is ridiclious hard even on the easy setting. One that requires you to have built up your ship immensely, but how are you able when the game forces you to run through the sectors?
Which brings up my next complaint of FTL is the lack of a save game feature. Sure their is a Save & Quit option, but the moment you load this save up its deleted, and if you die you restart from the beginning.
I heard so much about FTL from friends and reviews, and looked forward to playing it, but I am confused how it is so popular with the lack of a save game feature, forced skippage of exploration, and topped up with a overly difficult and cheap boss fight.
Had those last three issues not existed I would give FTL a 9/10 for sure, but because of these issues I give it a 6/10. Its a good game with so much potential that is just sucked right out because of really poor design ideas.
Hopefully if there is a FTL2, they will allow us nerds to explore the galaxy more without being forced to die over and over.
I would only recommend this game for those really big fans of sci-fi, and micro manage genre who like to die over and over.

Generally a well made game and a welcome return to good turn based mechanics.  Combat, progression and equipment aspects are very generic but well made. There is some voice acting in the game - of not very impressive quality and since otherwise, this game is a read-dialogue based, I wish it instead stuck with 100% read.  Unfortunately, dialogues and story line, after about 10 hours into the game for me, feel a bit weak - it does not grab and hold you and kinda feels too generic and appears to be recycled material from other routine titles of the RPG genre (e.g. a hero with no past will save a world with bare-bones lore populated with humans, orcs, elves, etc  - not creative enough to engage; characters are two-dimmesional and difficult to care about).  All in all, although I would recommend this game, I would not give it a glowing review  - like the RPG genre in the whole, this game has been affected by stagnation, there is not enough innovation in the game and the story is anemic.  Admitedly an RPG is very time consuming to make, so the developers are to be commended on their product.  The reason why I do recommend this game is because RPGs are a dying genre and have been heavily diluted in the past years with hack-and-slash pseudo RPG titles, and there are just not enoug titles out there - so this one comes welcome.

After 113 hours of play, I finally finished this game. That means a lot - I usually tire of most games after at most 20 hours, even if they are engaging and interesting. I enjoyed every minute of Divinity: Original Sin.
The story is grand but not contorted (I'm looking at you, Final Fantasy XIII), so you actually care about what happens next. The characters have personality, and you are responsible for shaping those personalities as a player during dialogues. The battle tactics are great, something you otherwise never see in the RPG genre. The item specs are meaningfully deeper than just DPS, so choosing gear is actually interesting and deserving of thought. The world is large and open - parts where you're not meant to be are usually closed to you solely by virtue of difficulty, not by invisible walls or other plot mechanisms. Most goals can be achieved by several different means, ranging from the typical choices of combat, sneaking or persuation, to more exotic solutions like obtaining unreachable keys using telekinesis or teleporting around obstacles using magic. The only negative I can think of is the music, which could have been better.
In summary, this is the best game I've played recently, and is among the very best games I've ever played.

If you're reformatting soon and don't mind the UPLAY issue, here's a review:
Child of Light is a platform game more unique than most. The game's main character (Aurora) has a 3D model in a 2D world. If you have issues in depth perception, this game might be challenging. I went through my first playthrough in about 12 hours. There are still things to do when the game is done, if you're into that sort of thing.
Controls are simple. Up, down, left, right. Combat is turn based with a timer on the bottom that can be manipulated through stats or your faerie. JRPG elements are easy to spot with element weaknesses and resistances. There is a learning curve, however. Typical fights do not require a lot of manipulation or understanding of the timer beneath the characters; however, boss fights are not forgiving and will shrek you if you don't understand the combat system. The learning curve, in this situation, actually resembles something more of an EKG graph. Some boss battles are stupidly easy, and others just involve you Interrupt Locking for 15 minutes.
Storyline is...interesting. Not fantastic, not awful. There are some parts of it that do not make sense from a logical perspect othat than, "because we have to move the story along". Specifically, Aurora's father and his state of affairs at all times. Not to spoil anything, but there are some very obvious "plot twists" that take far too long to reveal themselves. You can literally see the coming from a mile away. Like. 5 minutes into the game  ---> 8 hours later "plot twist revealed".
Characters each have their own personalities, although there's nothing solid or memorable about any of them. I wouldn't call them cookie-cutter, but they're not going to leave an impact on your like GlaDOS would.
Soundtrack is great. Absolutely no complaints there.
Overall flow of the game is about an 8/10. There's some graphical issues (where the heck does her hair keep going in fight scenes?) and sometimes unit collision on start of fights bugs out and you can't always tell when you're going to start with an advantage or get "Ambushed" status. If you're a completionist, I think you could probably get all of the hidden loot and memories in about 20 hours.
That being said, I wouldn't buy this game full price due to how short it was. Definitely worth playing, but I couldn't justify spending more than $7 on it.

When I was spending a year away from my regular school at my local community college, I always hung out in a room on campus where there were guys playing YuGiOh, Vanguard, emulators via a Nintendo Wii, and one guy always playing various fighting games.
There were 3 I remember the most, Tekken 6, BlazBlue (Don't remember which one though), and this game. I played it with him a few times, liked what I saw, but I couldn't get my hands on it, lack of a Playstation to put the disc into and all that. So, when I woke up to see that this game got released on steam and I had a coupon given to me because of some cross-promotion with Skullgirls (another phenomenal fighter), I spent little time adding the money to my steam wallet to pick this one up.
We've got a fun roster of colorful characters from various Nitro+ series, but I only immediately recognized 3 of them. Saber from Fate/Zero, Super Sonico because I spend too much time in the gutters of the internet, and Saya, who I am amused is in a game on steam considering the content of her native game. Everyone else is a mystery to me, and while that is a turn off for plenty of people (games like Tatsunoko vs. Capcom and Melty Blood have the same issue), the fighting is so good that I don't think it matters.
The fighting in this game is some of the best I've experienced, with silky smooth controls, a lot of opportunities for mix-ups, recovering is surprisingly easy to accomplish compared to most fighters I've played, and solid mechanics. You can call in one of your two chosen assist characters with the simple push of a button (which I assume depends on the controller), you can activate this sort of cancel that refills some of your health and rapidly increases your special gague, there's even a dodge of sorts, something that you don't see too often in fighting games.
The online even works really well, assuming your opponent has a good signal. I played a few matches against 2 or 3 opponents with a good signal, and I had virtually no input lag, minimal slowdown, and barely any freezes, and I'm stuck on dorm wifi at the time of writing.
The keyboard controls are mostly customizable, you can change everything except for the movement keys (ASDW for player 1, arrow keys for player 2). Controller compatability is there (as it should be), but I have no idea how many controllers are compatible. I have a 360 controller and it works perfectly (well, as perfectly as it can since the controller is not conducive to fighters), so those options are there.
There is a big flaw however, and its one that will drive away anyone who isn't a fighting game enthusiast. This game is not beginner friendly. There are no tutorials of any kind to help you learn how each character plays so you can figure out which one fits you best. Video tutorials exist, but most people aren't going to look those up. So if you're considering buying this, just note that figuring out who you're good at is a crapshoot unless you look up external sources.
Other than that though, this is a solid fighting game and another wonderful addition to my collection.

Oh wow. I have just finished my first play through of The Banner Saga. It is passed midnight, I have to be up early tomorrow but I just couldn't stop playing. Tired tomorrow? Still worth it! But you must forgive me if this review seems a little hysterical. It is rather late but I just had to get my thoughts down while it is still fresh.
I feel I must break down my review into categories to help me better explain just why I loved this game.
First and foremost:
Visuals
I cannot lie that the distinct art style is what first drew me to this title. It is just breathtaking. Every scene, every character is beautifully drawn that I just could not bear to look away. Even during combat the locations and characters maintained their style. As the caravan journeys across the lands you see magnificent Godstones, carved homages to the dead Gods, the detail is amazing. The artists truly put a lot of love and effort into this game, and it shows. If they ever decided to make an animated feature film for the lore of this series I would ecstatically buy it! Seriously if you are a fan of art and animation this title should be picked up for that alone!
The music
I was lucky to pick this game up when it was on sale so I decided to upgrade and get the soundtrack as well. I am so glad I did. If you think the art is beautiful wait until you hear the beautiful music, composed by Austin Wintory. It adds such a beautiful ambiance to each scene. Giving you a sense of dread, comfort and awe as you pass each village and mountain. I found it never took over the scenes to the point of distraction though so never fear, it is not the type of soundtrack that you find painfully distracting while looking for the mute button.
Combat
Now it’s time for full disclosure. I have not played many strategy games, I played a little diablo back in the day, games like total war and Pillars of Eternity (another amazing title! Go check it out!) So I cannot say with absolute certainty that this is a sophisticated, complex strategic combat system, however I found that on normal difficulty the game was very fun and fairly easy to complete. If you are new to this style of game, this title is not intimidating and a good introduction into strategy.
Player choice
Now this I loved. I adore RPGs that give you decent choice. Especially if you can never be certain if the choice is the ‘right’ one. Do you let these random men into your caravan or send them away? Do you stop and help a person or be on your way? Do you side with person A? Or Person B?  Just what are the consequences? I made a decision on day 3 in game, seemed like a fair choice at the time, All seems well until sometime around day 90 that the consequences finally played out. Each choice has weight to it and no decision should be made lightly, sometimes even the obvious choice may not be the right one.  Who lives? Who dies? Well that depends on you doesnt it?
Levelling and resources
Now this is a balancing act! Levelling and resources use ‘renown’. Resources keep your people alive, Levelling keeps you alive in battle, winning battles gives you renown. Do you level up your character? Or wait to buy more supplies so your people and soldiers don’t starve to death? Each has their consequences but I found it fun to try and manage it all.
Lore and characters
I adored the characters in this game! The lore was just enthralling. I found myself wanting to read everything and learn as much as I could about the dead Gods and the Varl. It really is beautiful and interesting so I advise you to pay attention!
This game is a solid 9½/10. Why does it lose half a point? Well there is one thing that annoyed me.
The final boss fight. Don’t worry this is a spoiler free review. All I can say is that there was a tremendous difficulty spike. It angered me so much at one point I was tempted to lower the difficulty. Luckily I persevered and managed to finish the game without doing so. So don’t give up! But this was the only thing that bothered me in over 12 hours of gameplay.
All in all I had a wonderful time, I heartily recommend this beautiful, enthralling game. I can’t wait for the sequel to be released!

I played this game about half-way in so far, and I can only recommend it.
It has an beautiful artstyle, an interesting story and generaly an incredibly well done atmosphere.
Many negative reviews critisize the combat system. However, I do not think the unique combat system of this game is a flaw. It's an authentic design choice, making Banner Saga an interesting alternative to the "usual" RBS.
Especialy on hard mode it becomes quite challenging, considering you will likely lose units from it, it adds to the strategic choices you have to take outside of the battle. Will you rest some more, to get you heroes back up, allthough you might soon run out of supplies? Or will you march on regardless, hoping that you can avoid fights for now? Or maybe you got some more heroes, which can substitute for the missing ones, while they tend to their wounds.
Nope. Can't say I find the combat system "flawed" or "broken". It's an unique and interesting distinct flavour, working well together with the game as a whole.

A pretty great game if you have a ton of spare time / leave your computer on or just like having a ton of things to do.
I've only played for a few days worth at the moment with a level 37 sorc and a 17 maehwa and I'm sad to say half the time I spent playing was doing crafting, gathering, cooking, house decorating and making money. I'm not even close to the end game where PvP and advanced PvE is supposed to be an entirely new game but I already love it.
So what can you do in this game?
You can do the typical MMO thing where you follow the quests and keep steadily levelling OR you can simply take the two daily login rewards that give you either 200% combat experience for an hour or 300% combat exp for an hour and a half, 200% being 30min. You don't even need to quest to level up in this game. Quests are there however to increase your inventory space and teach game mechanics so it is worth doing them even when overleveled.
If you get sick of killing mob after mob you can go ahead and do one of the many Lifeskills, gathering, cooking, alchemy, hunting, horse taming, farming and even sailing later on. Some of these skills go together like gathering can give you ingredients for farming cooking and alchemy, but even sailing and crafting countless items for houses and gear. The further you do these skills you can use better tools which make you do it even faster and better every day. Fishing for example gets reduction in time that you get fish bites, making AFK farming even greater.
But what if you're tired of that as well? Theres even Player Housing in the game. You can buy houses which you can't go in but to make crafting areas for your NPC Workers, or storage slots and much more or you can just buy a Residence which allows you to build. You'll have to buy and craft furniture from around the entire game world however and furniture is weighty and expensive, meaning the bigger house you have = the more time and effort required. When I completed my first floor of my three story house though I just felt immersed.
The real great thing about this game is immersion though, you can just sit back and hit T to auto run and then CTRL U to hide the UI and take some amazing pictures. Usually when a game has amazing graphics they have awful combat, but this game has excellent combat which allows you to combo pretty much every ability together.
The best part? It's not even £20, or £10. It's practically a free MMORPG that has more content than most MMOs.

I spent 2.1 hours on this game. I got a refund of the 5,99 euro I spent on it while it had a 40% sale. Now if I could get a refund of my time too that'd be great.
Yes, 2.1 hours might be far from what an MMO needs in order to show of the best of it, but I just could not handle the over the top artstyle, the same combat system I have seen in almost every asian mmo I have played so far, the very annoying tutorial at the start that treats me like I am an idiot.
The game pulls the extreme stripper armor for women like every mmorpg does now (mainly asian mmos!). Sure it might be nice to look at a "sexy" woman but it has gotten kinda overused by now. It is kind of like this: Constantly get something (or in this case, show cleavage and "sexy" animations) until you become used to it and it loses it's effect, or rarely show something and appreciate it much more.
Combat animations looks more like some typical anime fight where the characters make 3 billion flips until they hit their opponent rather than an actual decent fight where "player A swings sword, sword hits player B" instead of "Player A swings sword, then does 9 backflips while talking about their past as player B dodges all of player A's attacks at mach 9001 speed".
I like the aesthetics, the spawn area actually looks somewhat like an actual place on earth (besides the fantasy stuff).
I like the very open character customization (Aside from the class-gender lock and the fact that you could make yourself a giant but head could not be resized, resulting in a giant with a tiny head).
I like the controls, they are VERY smooth. I especially love the camera controls and the sprint mechanic.
I ran this on a GTX 970, Intel Core i5 CPU 650 3.20 GHz with 8 RAM. My computer can generally handle most heavy games with no problem. I have run GTA V with almost max graphics with no apparent frame drops. This game make me drop to 30 FPS on medium settings in a low population area. Everything renders very oddly ingame, especially the grass as it kept flickering and disappearing when I was 5 meters away from it. I tried to lower resolution down to the lowest possible but it kept flickering, I don't know what the problem was with Black Desert Online, but it felt very disorienting.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Generally I feel like Black Desert Online is an arcade MMO due to the easy mode treatment, fancy cosplay (and skimpy) clothing and the over the top combat animations. It has some problems with graphics as it made my head spin.
I might be wrong due to me playing for such a short time but early impressions needs to be good, right? Had the game shown a lot more dignity and had treated me like I am older than 9 years old, I might have spent 21 hours instead of 2.1 hours as my test run.
The way Diablo 3 should have been.
